source_issues.title: ACP: conversations cannot be resumed after sandbox restart (session_id is not persisted)

source_issues.title: Opencode GO kimi k2.6 return usage completions less than reasoning

signals.topic: Runtime container startup failure due to missing micromamba in default runtime:latest image
signals.summary: The default SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE (runtime:latest) uses miniforge3 instead of micromamba, causing the runtime container to fail to start immediately upon launch. Users cannot initiate any agent session.
aliases: runtime container fails to start micromamba
signals.review_reason: Three identical reports confirm a complete main-flow block: users cannot start any agent session because the runtime container immediately crashes on launch. The default image tag is misconfigured (miniforge3 vs micromamba). No workaround is available without manual image override, which average users cannot discover.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Runtime container fails to start - micromamba not found in runtime:latest

The default SANDBOX_RUNTIME_CONTAINER_IMAGE is set to ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:latest which uses miniforge3 (not micromamba). However the code expects micromamba. Workaround: use ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/runtime:0.42-nikolaik

signals.topic: MCP server env block from /settings/mcp UI not injected into spawned subprocess, breaking all MCP tool executions
signals.summary: User-configured environment variables in the MCP server settings UI are silently dropped before reaching the spawned MCP subprocess. MCP tools register correctly but fail at execution time with 'Missing required environment variables' because env vars are empty.
aliases: MCP environment variables not passed to subprocess
MCP env block UI not reaching spawned process
signals.review_reason: A core feature (MCP server integration) is completely broken in cloud deployments. Tools register but cannot execute because required env vars are stripped before reaching the subprocess. User documented k8s-level diagnostic evidence showing zero env vars in the runtime pod. User had to bypass OpenHands entirely and run the audit directly over Tailscale. This is a main-flow failure with clear user impact and cost (failed workflow).

source_issues.title: MCP stdio env block from /settings/mcp UI not received by spawned subprocess (cloud-1.25.1)
source_issues.evidence: MCP servers configured via /settings/mcp UI register tool names correctly (agent sees them) but the env block does NOT reach the spawned subprocess. The subprocess fails on its own preconditions: 'Missing required environment variables' because it sees an empty env. Diagnostic: runtime pod has zero env vars matching the configured secrets; no mcp_clickhouse process is running. Likely related to SDK redaction work that sanitizes secret-bearing fields during serialization.

signals.topic: Bitbucket provider authentication completely broken - API token authentication fails on both self-hosted and cloud
signals.summary: Bitbucket App Passwords are deprecated; Bitbucket now requires API tokens. OpenHands still uses the old auth format and all Bitbucket authentication attempts fail with 401 Unauthorized, blocking core repository integration.
signals.review_reason: A core platform feature (Bitbucket repository integration) is completely non-functional for all users on both self-hosted and cloud deployments. Bitbucket's deprecation of App Passwords is an external change; OpenHands has not updated its auth handler. The 401 Unauthorized logs confirm repeated failures. This is a persistent main-flow block with no in-product workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Bitbucket provider authentication broken (API tokens not working)
source_issues.evidence: Bitbucket App Passwords are deprecated. Bitbucket now requires API tokens. OpenHands still appears to rely on the old authentication format. All attempted authentication formats fail (username:api_token, email:api_token, x-token-auth:api_token). Server logs show: Status error on bitbucket_data_center API: Redirect response '302 Found' for url 'https://bitbucket.org/rest/api/1.0/repos' redirecting to /account/signin/. Affects both self-hosted and cloud. Blocks core use case of OpenHands (repository integration).

signals.topic: Switching between OpenHands and ACP agent types causes 500 error on settings save, breaking agent reconfiguration
signals.summary: When a user switches agent_kind (OpenHands agent ACP agent) in Settings, Settings.update() deep-merges the agent settings blob without replacing the union-typed base, causing stale fields from the old type to leak into the new type's schema and triggering HTTP 500.
aliases: settings update fails on agent type change
signals.review_reason: Agent type switching is a key feature of OpenHands (supporting both OpenHands agents and external ACP agents like Claude Code, Codex, Gemini). The 500 error makes this feature completely unusable once a user has saved settings for both types. Though only 1 issue, the bug is precisely reproduced with a clear root cause and affects a first-class product feature. Downgraded to P1 because count=1 and it's an edge case within the agent-switching flow rather than a universal block.

source_issues.title: fix(settings): switching agent_kind leaks stale fields across discriminated union types
source_issues.evidence: Switching between the OpenHands agent and an ACP agent (Settings -> Agent) throws a 500 'Something went wrong storing settings' on the return trip (ACP -> OpenHands). Root cause: Settings.update() deep-merges agent_settings_diff but doesn't replace the base when agent_kind changes, leaving stale fields from the old union member. Reproducer confirmed: start with OpenHands agent -> switch to ACP -> save -> switch back to OpenHands -> 500.

signals.topic: ACP conversations cannot be resumed after cloud sandbox restart - session state lives only in ephemeral sandbox filesystem
signals.summary: ACP agent sessions (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) lose their session_id and working directory after a cloud sandbox recycle. The SDK correctly implements session/load but depends on state that lives in the sandbox filesystem, which is wiped on recycle. Users lose all conversation history and must start over.
aliases: ACP session lost after sandbox restart
ACP conversation resume fails after sandbox recycle
signals.review_reason: Cloud sandbox restarts are a normal operational occurrence (agent-server crashes, pod rescheduling). After restart, all ACP conversation state is lost and users must start fresh — losing all context, tool call provenance, and sandbox filesystem state. This is a recurring user experience failure for cloud ACP users. The issue proposes concrete solutions; it is not a theoretical concern.

source_issues.title: ACP: conversations cannot be resumed after sandbox restart (session_id is not persisted)
source_issues.evidence: ACP conversations cannot be resumed after a cloud sandbox is recycled. The acp_session_id and acp_session_cwd live in base_state.json on the sandbox filesystem (LocalFileStore), which is wiped on recycle. ACP server's own session files (~/.claude/projects/, ~/.codex/, ~/.gemini/) are also in the sandbox $HOME and are lost. The durable cloud event store has the transcript but the session state needed for ACP session/load is gone. Affects all three ACP agents: claude-agent-acp, codex-acp, and gemini.

Count=3 meets frequency threshold; single-repo but high-impact (Agent Builder is a primary workflow). Downgraded to P1 (not P0) because count=3 with no additional corroborating evidence beyond the issues themselves.

signals.topic: QQ Bot SSRF guard blocks bots.qq.com under Clash/V2Ray TUN-mode fake-IP DNS (China users)
signals.summary: In mainland China, popular proxy tools (Clash, V2RayN, Mihomo, etc.) default to TUN-mode + fake-IP DNS, which resolves public hostnames to the 198.18.0.0/15 benchmark block. OpenClaw's SSRF guard rejects these as private IPs, causing every QQ Bot API call (token refresh, WebSocket connect) to be blocked. The bot enters a forever-disconnect loop. This affects the majority of Chinese users who run a proxy, even with TUN enabled by default in popular proxy GUIs.
aliases: QQ Bot blocked by SSRF under proxy TUN mode China
signals.review_reason: P1: Chinese market represents a significant portion of users. The issue has detailed root cause, reproducible steps, and a confirmed fix in a downstream fork. The bot completely fails to connect due to SSRF false positives — this is a functional blocker for users in mainland China using standard proxy configurations.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QQ Bot SSRF guard blocks bots.qq.com under Clash/V2Ray TUN-mode fake-IP DNS (China)
source_issues.evidence: Detailed root cause analysis: fetchWithSsrFGuard called without policy on qqbot.token and qqbot.api paths; reproduces on all major Chinese proxy tools with TUN default; bot enters forever-disconnect loop; verified fix in portable fork with end-to-end test under Clash TUN mode.

signals.topic: RealtimeAgent exposes execute_python_code tool to remote WebSocket users, enabling unauthorized server-side Python code execution
signals.summary: RealtimeAgent's WebSocket endpoint forwards model-produced tool calls to execute_python_code without sandbox or approval boundary, allowing any remote WebSocket client to trigger arbitrary server-side Python execution when this tool is exposed in a session.
aliases: Remote code execution via RealtimeAgent WebSocket tool call
Unauthorized server-side Python execution via exposed execute_python_code tool
WebSocket tool call lacks containment boundary for execute_python_code
signals.review_reason: Confirmed RCE-level security vulnerability with reproducible proof-of-concept (marker file creation confirmed). Any remote WebSocket client can trigger server-side Python code execution when execute_python_code is exposed in a RealtimeAgent session. This is a direct, high-severity user impact: unauthenticated remote code execution on the service host. No sandbox or approval boundary exists on the validated code path (RealtimeAgent._acting -> Toolkit.call_tool_function -> execute_python_code).

source_issues.title: [Bug]:RealtimeAgent tool call path allows remote users to trigger server-side Python execution when execute_python_code is exposed

Affects AgentScope 1.0.18, 1.0.19, 1.0.19.post1. No sandbox, approval, or containment boundary between WebSocket input and server-side Python execution.

signals.topic: CopilotKit/AG-UI integration broken: context not passed, tools not triggered, infinite loop on external execution
signals.summary: The AG-UI adapter in agno/os/interfaces/agui/router.py has three interrelated bugs that collectively break the CopilotKit integration: (1) run_input.context from CopilotKit frontend is not passed to Agent.arun(), so useCopilotReadable context is silently discarded; (2) frontend tools declared via useComponent/useHumanInTheLoop in CopilotKit are never extracted from the AG-UI HTTP request, so they never fire; (3) with external_execution=true tools, the agent only receives the last message instead of full conversation history, causing infinite re-triggering via agent.continue_run(). All three share the same root file (router.py lines 33-61). The integration is confirmed broken on Agno 2.6.4 with @ag-ui/agno 0.0.3 and CopilotKit 1.56-1.57.
aliases: AG-UI adapter does not pass context to agent
AG-UI tools not extracted from HTTP request
signals.review_reason: Three distinct GitHub issues (7805, 7802, 7801) sharing the same root file (agno/os/interfaces/agui/router.py) collectively demonstrate that the entire CopilotKit integration via AG-UI is non-functional: (1) CopilotKit frontend context is silently discarded so agents cannot see frontend page data; (2) frontend CopilotKit tools (useComponent, useHumanInTheLoop) are never extracted from HTTP requests; (3) external_execution tools cause infinite loops. These are main-flow blocking for any user trying to use Agno with CopilotKit, which is an officially documented integration path. All three have confirmed reproduction steps and concrete evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug] AG-UI adapter receives context but does not pass run_input.context to Agent.arun()
source_issues.evidence: CopilotKit useCopilotReadable context visible in CopilotKit Inspector and in /api/copilotkit payload but silently discarded by agno router. Agent responds 'I can't see your page/content' despite context existing. Reproduction with working frontend code and full payload shown in issue.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Tools with external_execution = true integrated with CopilotKit are triggered infinitely
source_issues.evidence: Infinite loop confirmed: 'sayHello' frontend tool triggered infinitely with CopilotKit. Root cause: agent receives only last message, not full history, so on continue_run() it re-triggers the tool. Reproduction steps provided with CopilotKit Quickstart.

source_issues.title: [Bug] AG-UI interface tools are not integrated with the Agent
source_issues.evidence: Frontend tools via useComponent and useHumanInTheLoop never fire. Intercepted HTTP request shows tools in AG-UI payload but debug mode shows agent has no tools registered. Direct link to failing code in router.py lines 33-61.

signals.topic: ChromaDb async_insert/async_upsert blocks the asyncio event loop by calling sync Rust code directly
signals.summary: ChromaDb._async_upsert and async_insert call synchronous chromadb.api.rust._upsert/_add directly on the asyncio event loop, starving all other coroutines. This causes health check timeouts, frozen HTTP long-polls, and stalled queue drains in long-running async services. py-spy evidence confirms the main thread is blocked in Rust code. Other async methods in the same file already use asyncio.to_thread as a pattern.
aliases: ChromaDb async methods blocking event loop
sync Rust write on asyncio loop thread
signals.review_reason: Single issue but with exceptionally strong evidence: py-spy stack trace showing asyncio main thread blocked in synchronous Rust code, multiple concrete production symptoms (health check timeouts, frozen HTTP long-polls, stalled queue drains), and a linked fix PR (#7711). The bug is in the public async API of a core database integration (ChromaDb), causing real service degradation in async applications. The same async-by-name-only pattern exists in other vector DB integrations, suggesting broader risk.

source_issues.title: [Bug] ChromaDb async upsert/insert blocks the asyncio event loop (sync Rust write on the loop thread)
source_issues.evidence: py-spy snapshot confirms main asyncio thread blocked in chromadb.api.rust._upsert. Real production symptoms documented: HTTP long-polls freeze triggering watchdog timeouts; inflated time-to-first-token on streamed model responses; queue drains backing up. Issue links to PR #7711 with fix. Workaround via asyncio.to_thread exists. Also affects Knowledge.ainsert path.

signals.topic: Google Drive allDrives search silently returns incomplete results without exposing incompleteSearch flag
signals.summary: GoogleDriveTools.search_files() with corpora='allDrives' does not request or return the Drive API incompleteSearch flag. When Google Drive cannot search all drives, it sets incompleteSearch=true but callers receive no indication, leading to silently incorrect search results for shared drive queries.
aliases: Drive API incompleteSearch missing from field mask
signals.review_reason: This is a data integrity bug where Google Drive shared drive searches can silently return incomplete results without any user indication. The incompleteSearch flag from the Drive API is a documented safety mechanism that Agno's GoogleDriveTools explicitly omits from the field mask. Users relying on allDrives corpora for comprehensive search have no way to detect when results are partial. The issue describes a real API contract gap, not just a missing feature.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Google Drive allDrives searches do not expose incompleteSearch
source_issues.evidence: Google Drive API documents that incompleteSearch=true occurs for allDrives corpora when all corpora could not be searched. Agno field mask omits incompleteSearch. Callers silently receive incomplete results with no indication. Reproduction steps provided with GoogleDriveTools configuration.

signals.topic: Milvus vector DB with contents_db: insert/update fails with field length exceeded and type mismatch errors

Additionally, the upsert call uses a partial body that only works on Milvus 2.6.2+. The user had to manually patch installed agno source code as a workaround.

signals.review_reason: Milvus + contents_db combination causes insert/update operations to fail with two distinct errors, both producing full stack traces. signals.topic: Reading PDF/binary files corrupts Amazon Bedrock sessions irreversibly
signals.summary: When the Read tool is used on a PDF or other binary file with Amazon Bedrock provider, the session becomes permanently unrecoverable. The binary content is stored as a file-data tool result which Bedrock's AI SDK does not support in subsequent LLM calls, causing every following turn to fail with an unrecoverable error.
aliases: binary file read corrupts Bedrock session
PDF read causes unrecoverable session error on Bedrock
signals.review_reason: Reading a PDF via the Read tool permanently corrupts the session for Amazon Bedrock users. The session becomes unrecoverable, blocking the main workflow. This is a severe UX failure where a common operation (reading a binary file) makes the entire session unusable.

source_issues.title: Reading a PDF file via the Read tool corrupts session when using Amazon Bedrock — unrecoverable error
source_issues.evidence: After reading a PDF file, every subsequent LLM call in the session fails immediately with an unrecoverable error. The session cannot be resumed. Root cause: Bedrock's AI SDK does not support file-data content parts in tool results.

signals.topic: Remote workspace directory leak causes session list to collapse to empty black screen
signals.summary: When using a custom WorkspaceAdapter with remote workspaces, the local machine's directory path leaks into the proxied request via the ?directory= query parameter. The remote instance cannot resolve this path, falls back to worktree '/', and the sessionListQuery returns an empty list. Users see a black screen with no sessions.
aliases: workspaceProxyURL directory query leaks to remote
remote workspace session list empty after warp
signals.review_reason: Remote workspace sessions collapse to a black screen with zero visible sessions after warp. The bug is well-documented with a root cause chain traced from SDK header rewriting through proxy routing to store reconciliation. A one-line fix is identified but the impact on users of custom WorkspaceAdapters is a complete workflow block.

source_issues.title: Bug: workspaceProxyURL forwards local 'directory' query to remote workspace, breaking sessionListQuery
source_issues.evidence: The SDK rewrites x-opencode-directory headers into ?directory= query. workspaceProxyURL strips ?workspace= but not ?directory= before proxying. Remote resolves the non-existent local path, falls back to worktree '/', causing path.relative() to produce a bogus path. sessionListQuery returns [], the store is emptied, and the session route renders a black screen.

signals.topic: Electron desktop sidecar fails to load npm plugins due to peer dependency resolution error
signals.summary: After updating to Electron-based OpenCode Desktop v1.14.39, npm plugins with @opencode-ai/plugin as a peer dependency fail to load. The sidecar's dependency installer resolves @opencode-ai/plugin as @opencode-ai/plugin@local which doesn't exist on npm, causing cascade install failures and plugin loading failures.
aliases: npm plugins fail to load desktop electron
peer dependency @opencode-ai/plugin resolves as local and fails
signals.review_reason: All npm plugins with the @opencode-ai/plugin peer dependency fail to load in the Electron desktop app. The install process incorrectly treats a host-provided module as an npm package. This blocks the plugin ecosystem on the desktop platform.

source_issues.title: Electron sidecar: npm plugins fail to load — peer dep @opencode-ai/plugin resolves as @local
source_issues.evidence: Plugin fails to load with NpmInstallFailedError: @opencode-ai/plugin@local: No matching version found. The sidecar treats the host-provided peer dependency as an npm package to install. Affects all npm plugins with that peer dep on the desktop Electron build.

signals.topic: Archived sessions permanently disappear with no UI to view or restore them
signals.summary: The archive session action (mod+shift+backspace) marks a session as archived and removes it from the sidebar, but there is no UI to view or restore archived sessions. The action is destructive with no undo path — once archived, the session is gone from the UI permanently despite the data remaining intact in the SQLite database.
signals.review_reason: Archiving a session permanently removes it from the UI with no recovery path. The data is preserved in the database but inaccessible. This is a destructive action with no undo — users lose access to their session history with no warning or recovery mechanism.

source_issues.title: Archived sessions disappear permanently with no way to view or restore them
source_issues.evidence: Backend stores archived sessions in SQLite but frontend explicitly filters them out in three places with no way to access them. The archive action has no undo and no recovery path. Affects all app variants (Web, TUI, Desktop).

signals.topic: kimi-k2.6 via opencode-go provider returns negative completion token counts, corrupting session load
signals.summary: The opencode-go provider for kimi-k2.6 returns completion_tokens that are less than reasoning_tokens, resulting in negative output token values stored in the database. When the session is loaded, the tui assumes values >= 0, causing a schema validation error (Expected >= 0, got -46) and preventing the session from loading at all.
aliases: negative output tokens prevent session loading
kimi k2.6 completions less than reasoning tokens
signals.review_reason: Sessions using kimi-k2.6 through opencode-go cannot be loaded at all due to negative token values in the database. The schema validation fails at the API level, blocking the session entirely. This affects core workflow persistence.

source_issues.title: Opencode GO kimi k2.6 return usage completions less than reasoning
source_issues.evidence: Session load fails with HTTP 400: SchemaError: Expected a value greater than or equal to 0, got -46. Four messages have negative output tokens. The session cannot be loaded. Root cause: k2.6 returns completions < reasoning tokens, and OpenCode stores the negative value without validation.

signals.topic: embedded reflect.Type prevents Go linker dead-code elimination, causing inflated binary sizes
signals.summary: The SDK embeds reflect.Type in exported structs, which breaks Go's linker dead-code elimination (--trimpath / -l flag). This forces entire SDK code into user binaries even when only a fraction of SDK functionality is used, significantly increasing binary size especially impactful for CLI tools and WASM targets.
aliases: reflect.Type embedded breaks dead code elimination
linker dead code elimination disabled by SDK types
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user pain point: the embedded reflect.Type breaks Go linker dead-code elimination, causing measurable binary bloat. The user (from Stainless-es infra) explicitly reports this as a blocking issue for their projects. While count=1 limits priority to P2, the impact is real and non-trivial — dead-code elimination failures directly increase deployment costs and download times, and are particularly severe for CLI/WASM targets where binary size is critical.

source_issues.title: bug: embedded reflect.Type breaks Go linker dead-code elimination
source_issues.evidence: User (ofek-frame from Stainless-es infra) explicitly reports that using this SDK disabled dead-code elimination on their projects, leading to increased binary sizes. Issue references a cross-SDK (openai/openai-go) root cause investigation at https://github.com/openai/openai-go/issues/609.

signals.topic: Java quickstart documentation is non-functional — missing classpath setup and references non-existent Maven version
signals.summary: The official Java quickstart page instructs users to run `javac`/`java` without classpath configuration, causing compilation failure, and references Maven version `2.20.0` which does not exist on Maven Central. This completely blocks all new Java SDK users from completing the Get Started flow.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocker for all new Java SDK users. The quickstart page (the primary onboarding path) is broken in two independent ways: missing dependency setup and incorrect Maven version. Evidence is clear and self-contained in the issue body.

source_issues.title: Java quickstart docs: javac/java commands don't work without classpath setup, version 2.20.0 doesn't exist
source_issues.evidence: Docs tell users to run `javac QuickStart.java` and `java QuickStart` without any classpath setup. The QuickStart.java imports `com.anthropic.*` JARs that `javac` cannot resolve. Maven/Gradle snippets reference version 2.20.0 which returns 404 on Maven Central (latest is 2.26.0). Both issues together make the quickstart completely unusable for any new Java developer.

signals.topic: Structured output schema generator treats all Java fields as required, ignoring nullability — forces LLM to hallucinate values
signals.summary: When using StructuredMessageCreateParams with outputConfig(), the Java SDK's internal schema generator adds every class field to the JSON Schema `required` array regardless of nullability annotations (@Nullable, Optional<T>, @JsonProperty(required=false)). This causes Claude models to hallucinate placeholder values (e.g. string 'null', empty string, or dash) even when the field is semantically optional.
aliases: structured output schema required fields wrong
nullable fields treated as mandatory in schema generation
signals.review_reason: This directly breaks the core functionality of structured output: the feature works but produces wrong/misleading results because optional fields are incorrectly marked as required. The LLM is forced to hallucinate values to comply with an over-strict schema. User impact is clearly described with a reproducible code example.

source_issues.title: Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User provides concrete record example (LlmVerdictOutput with @jakarta.annotation.Nullable parentCaseNumber and Optional<Integer> ageAtIncident) — both fields still appear in the schema's required array. User reports LLM 'hallucinates' string 'null', empty string, or dash to satisfy schema constraints. Workarounds tried: @Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), Optional<T> — none work.

signals.topic: VS Code extension fails to load on Windows UNC/network paths (corporate environment)
signals.summary: Claude Code VS Code extension crashes on load when opening a folder from a UNC network path (e.g. \\server\share), throwing ENOENT errors referencing non-existent mapped drives. All workarounds (cache clear, reinstall, simplify settings) fail. Corporate users without admin rights to map drives are completely blocked from using the extension.
signals.review_reason: Extension load failure is a main-flow block. User is completely unable to use the extension on corporate network paths. All workarounds failed and there is no resolution path without admin access to map drives. Specific error evidence (ENOENT, realpathSync stack trace) confirms the crash.

source_issues.title: Claude Code Extension fails to load on network paths (UNC paths)
source_issues.evidence: Extension crashes with ENOENT on UNC paths. All workarounds failed. No admin rights to map drives means no resolution path.

signals.topic: VS Code extension fails to install on Windows (TypeError: invalid filename)
signals.summary: Claude Code extension version 2.1.129 fails to install on Windows due to a TypeError caused by a hardcoded Linux-style absolute path in the extension bundle (file:///home/runner/work/...). Users must downgrade to 2.1.28 to work around.
aliases: file URL path error on Windows
signals.review_reason: Extension installation failure is a complete block — users cannot use the extension at all on affected versions. The error shows a hardcoded Linux absolute path baked into the extension bundle, indicating a CI/build pipeline error that would affect all Windows users on that version.

source_issues.title: Claude Code extension for VSCode version 2.1.129 does not install correctly
source_issues.evidence: Extension fails to activate with TypeError on Windows. Workaround required downgrading to 2.1.28.

signals.topic: AsyncAnthropicVertex 404 errors on US/EU regions vs sync working correctly
signals.summary: AsyncAnthropicVertex uses a different endpoint base URL than the sync version for US and EU regions, resulting in 404 errors. Sync mode works fine with the same credentials/region, making async usage on Vertex AI with US/EU regions functionally broken.
signals.review_reason: Async Vertex AI is a core integration path for enterprise users on Google Cloud. The 404 error means async workflows are completely broken for US and EU regions while sync works — a clear functional regression. While the issue is closed, the underlying bug (wrong endpoint base URL) is a real runtime failure for any user relying on async Vertex AI.

source_issues.title: Async methods NOT working with US/EU regions on Vertex AI - Gets 404 on endpoints
source_issues.evidence: AsyncAnthropicVertex sends POST to wrong endpoint for US/EU regions (us-aiplatform.googleapis.com vs aiplatform.us.rep.googleapis.com). Sync works with same credentials. 404 confirmed.

signals.topic: Enterprise MDM: Keychain prompt reappears after every Claude Desktop update in Jamf-managed environments
signals.summary: After every MDM-managed update via Jamf Pro, users in enterprise environments without iCloud see a persistent Keychain prompt for 'Claude Key'. The prompt reappears after every update cycle, generating repeated helpdesk tickets. Pre-creating the keychain entry does not suppress the prompt.
aliases: Claude Desktop keychain reprompt after updates
signals.review_reason: Repeated UI prompt after every update is a significant UX degradation in enterprise environments, particularly for non-technical users and in regulated compliance contexts. The issue affects all 102 managed endpoints and generates repeated helpdesk tickets. Not P0 because clicking Cancel allows normal use.

source_issues.title: [Enterprise/MDM][Jamf Pro] Keychain prompt 'Claude Key' appears after every update in managed environments without iCloud
source_issues.evidence: 102 managed endpoints affected. Keychain prompt reappears after every update. Pre-creating the keychain entry via security add-generic-password does not suppress it. ISO 27001 / NIS2 regulated environment.

signals.topic: Prompt caching activates at 2048 tokens instead of documented 1024 for Claude Sonnet
signals.summary: Claude Sonnet prompt caching documentation states activation at 1024 tokens, but actual behavior requires ~2048 tokens for cache creation to trigger. Users relying on documented thresholds for cost optimization have cache misses and pay full input pricing for prefixes in the 1024–2047 range.
aliases: prompt caching token threshold documentation error
signals.review_reason: Documentation mismatch causes direct financial harm — users who size their prompts based on the documented 1024-token threshold pay full price for cache prefixes that don't actually trigger caching. This is a consistent, reproducible cost leakage affecting anyone optimizing for prompt caching on Sonnet.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching for Claude Sonnet appears to start at 2048 tokens instead of documented 1024
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction code shows 0 cache tokens at 1351 and 1464 input tokens. Only triggers at 2048+. Causes users to overpay due to incorrect documentation.

signals.topic: toolRunner drops defaultHeaders on follow-up requests in multi-turn tool use loops
signals.summary: In multi-turn tool use loops, toolRunner's internal follow-up API calls drop custom defaultHeaders (including auth headers), causing authentication failures when the SDK is used behind proxies/gateways like Cloudflare AI Gateway. Single-shot messages.create works fine; only toolRunner is affected. Users must manually re-implement the entire tool-use loop as a workaround.
aliases: defaultHeaders lost in tool execution loop
signals.review_reason: Confirmed SDK bug causing authentication failures on follow-up requests within the tool-use loop. Directly blocks the primary multi-turn tool-use workflow when using proxies or gateways. The error results in a hard API authentication failure (HTTP 400 authentication_error). The mandatory workaround is to completely re-implement the tool-use loop manually — a non-trivial engineering burden. Confirmed by Cloudflare team as an SDK bug affecting real production usage.

source_issues.title: `toolRunner` drops `defaultHeaders` on follow-up requests (breaks proxy/gateway setups)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed SDK bug — first API call includes defaultHeaders, follow-up calls in tool-use loop drop them, resulting in 'authentication_error: x-api-key header is required'. Cloudflare team confirmed this is an SDK-side bug. Breakage includes Cloudflare AI Gateway unified billing (cf-aig-authorization header). Workaround requires manually re-implementing the entire tool-use loop.

signals.topic: MCP servers: unreachable server causes entire multi-server request to fail with no optional flag or per-server timeout
signals.summary: When using mcp_servers in the Messages API (beta), a single unreachable MCP server (e.g., a flaky dev tunnel or ephemeral service) fails the entire atomic request. There is no per-server optional flag, no per-server timeout, and the error message does not identify the failing server in a structured way. This makes multi-server production deployments extremely fragile.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks production deployments that compose multiple MCP servers — a realistic and increasingly common pattern. A transient outage on one third-party MCP server takes down the entire tool call path, including healthy servers that were never even reached. The error message provides no actionable identification of which server failed, making automated recovery impossible. The underlying request demonstrates clear user impact: real-world reproduction with sanitized traces, and architectural reasoning ruling out client-side workarounds (SSRF, DNS rebinding, TOCTOU, false negatives). P1 (not P0) because the failure is confined to beta MCP server injection and a gateway decoupling pattern exists as an architectural alternative.

source_issues.title: API: mcp_servers[].optional flag + structured error for graceful degradation on unreachable injected MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction provided: two MCP servers configured, one reachable, one unreachable — entire request fails with HTTP 400 'Connection error while communicating with MCP server'. The healthy server is never reached. Error message is free-text and non-actionable — server name is not included, making bisect/retry unreliable. Affects any production deployment using multiple MCP servers (file system bridge + search backend + domain-specific tool servers). Cloudflare/ngrok/dev tunnels flap legitimately in production.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.6 returns empty content array when using output_config with json_schema format
signals.summary: Claude Opus 4.6 intermittently but near-consistently returns an empty content array when the request includes output_config with json_schema format. The model returns stop_reason=end_turn with 6 output tokens but zero content blocks. Workarounds exist (downgrade to Opus 4.5, enable thinking mode, or remove output_config) but are non-trivial for users who specifically need Opus 4.6 with structured output.
aliases: Opus 4.6 empty response with json_schema output
output_config json_schema causes empty content on Opus 4.6
signals.review_reason: Significant model/API behavior bug causing Opus 4.6 to silently return zero content while reporting a successful end_turn — the request appears to succeed but yields no usable output. This directly breaks structured output workflows that depend on json_schema validation. The 'almost always' reproduction rate means users cannot reliably use this feature combination. P1 rather than P0 because workarounds exist (model switch, thinking mode toggle) that don't require a breaking code change, and only the json_schema + Opus 4.6 combination is affected.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.6 returns empty content with output_config json_schema
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced almost all the time with a minimal repro payload provided. Model returns stop_reason=end_turn with output_tokens=6 but content=[] (empty array), meaning no usable response. Workarounds are model-level (switch to Opus 4.5, enable thinking mode) or feature-level (remove output_config), all of which are non-trivial for users relying on Opus 4.6 structured output. Full minimal repro payload included.

signals.topic: Memory resource leaks: anyio memory object stream and stderr task group cancel scope not cleaned up on query() completion
signals.summary: query.close() cancels the task group and closes the transport but leaves anyio memory object streams uncleaned. Additionally, SubprocessCLITransport's stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query completion, an incomplete fix of a known bug.
aliases: stderr task group cancel scope leak in SubprocessCLITransport
anyio memory object stream not cleaned up
signals.review_reason: Two separate memory/resource leaks on query completion (#859: anyio memory object streams; #810: stderr task group cancel scope). Both affect any long-running application using the SDK repeatedly — accumulated leaks degrade service stability over time. Both have known root causes and are reproducible.

source_issues.title: Resource Leak: anyio memory object stream associated with a query is leaked
source_issues.evidence: query.close() cancels task group and closes transport but leaves other resources (memory object streams) uncleaned, causing memory leaks on repeated query() calls.

source_issues.title: SubprocessCLITransport stderr task group leaks cancel scope on query() completion — same bug #454 / #776, fix #746 incomplete
source_issues.evidence: SubprocessCLITransport repeats the exact same anyio.create_task_group() anti-pattern that was partially fixed in PR #746 in a different file. Stderr task group cancel scope leaks on query completion.

signals.topic: Bundled Claude binary silently times out (60s) in Docker container environments due to protocol incompatibility
signals.summary: When claude_agent_sdk.query() runs inside a Docker container, the bundled claude binary (v2.1.121) fails to respond to control_request:initialize, causing a silent 60-second timeout with no error message, completely blocking the main SDK query flow.
aliases: bundled CLI protocol incompatibility in containers
silent 60s timeout on initialize in Docker
signals.review_reason: This blocks the primary SDK workflow (query()) with a silent 60-second timeout in Docker containers — a very common deployment environment for SDK users. The absence of any error message makes it extremely difficult to diagnose. Count=1 but impact is severe (main flow completely blocked).

source_issues.title: _bundled/claude v2.1.121 protocol-incompatible in container env (silent timeout on control_request:initialize)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced in vectorize-io/hindsight Docker image with detailed environment. SDK times out at 60s with no error. Workaround requires bind-mounting a newer host binary over SDK path.

signals.topic: API-key users silently unable to opt into 1-hour prompt cache TTL; bundled CLI predates ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H feature flag
signals.summary: API-key users of claude-agent-sdk-python cannot use the 1-hour prompt cache TTL because the bundled CLI version (2.1.105 in v0.1.59) predates the ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var, resulting in higher API costs and longer latency for all requests.
aliases: 1h prompt cache TTL not available to API-key users
API-key users stuck on 5m cache TTL
signals.review_reason: This causes direct cost loss (higher API token usage) and latency increase on every API call for all API-key users of the SDK. The bundled CLI being out of date with a missing feature flag means users silently pay more without knowing why.

source_issues.title: API-key users silently stuck on 5m cache TTL: bundled CLI in v0.1.59 predates ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H opt-in
source_issues.evidence: Bundled CLI 2.1.105 lacks ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var (added in CLI 2.1.108). API-key users cannot opt into 1h cache TTL, causing direct cost and latency impact on every API call.

signals.topic: SDK subprocess crashes during long-running sessions with heavy MCP polling; stderr swallowed and errors uninformative
signals.summary: During long agent sessions (60+ turns) with heavy MCP tool polling, the Claude CLI subprocess exits non-zero and the SDK surfaces only a generic Exception without the actual CLI stderr output, making diagnosis impossible.

uninformative error on long-running query with MCP tools
CLI subprocess crash during MCP polling

This directly blocks debugging of real CLI failures during production workloads, especially problematic for long-running agentic applications.

source_issues.title: SDK subprocess crash during long-running queries with heavy MCP polling — stderr swallowed, error message uninformative
source_issues.evidence: Long sessions (60+ turns) with heavy MCP polling cause CLI subprocess to exit non-zero. SDK shows only 'Exception: Command failed with exit code 1' with no stderr details.

source_issues.title: ProcessError exit_code/stderr stripped during error propagation; users see generic Exception with hard-coded placeholder
source_issues.evidence: ProcessError with structured exit_code and stderr fields is destroyed during propagation and re-raised as generic Exception. Users cannot see actual CLI output to diagnose failures.

signals.topic: query() with string prompt and mcp_servers fails with CLIConnectionError during MCP handshake
signals.summary: Calling query() with a string prompt and mcp_servers set still fails with CLIConnectionError: 'ProcessTransport is not ready for writing' during the MCP server handshake. This is a regression that has persisted across multiple versions.
aliases: MCP handshake fails with stdin closed on string prompts
ProcessTransport not ready during MCP handshake
signals.review_reason: This blocks a common use case: using string prompts together with MCP servers. The error (ProcessTransport not ready for writing) is a direct main-flow failure, not a degraded experience. MCP server integration is a key SDK feature.

source_issues.title: query() + mcp_servers: string-prompt branch closes stdin before MCP handshake, not fixed by #731
source_issues.evidence: At v0.1.33, string prompt + mcp_servers still fails with CLIConnectionError during MCP server handshake. Stdin is closed prematurely before MCP handshake completes.

signals.topic: Subprocess EPIPE crash during startup-crash race kills host process causing production downtime
signals.summary: When the Claude Code subprocess crashes during startup and the parent attempts a fresh-retry write to stdin within ~8ms, an uncaught EPIPE is raised. The error has no JS stack frame, bypassing typical error handlers, and exits the host process directly — causing full gateway downtime with orphaned sessions.
aliases: process kill on subprocess crash race
signals.review_reason: Production-main-incident-level impact: full gateway downtime, session loss, and job orphaning. The crash bypasses standard Node.js error handling because EPIPE arrives without a JS stack frame. Host applications without a defensive uncaughtException handler will crash silently. Only single-issue evidence but the severity is unambiguous — the reporter is a production platform team with real timestamps.

source_issues.title: Uncaught EPIPE from subprocess stdin write callback during startup-crash → fresh-retry race (v0.2.120)
source_issues.evidence: Production incident: EPIPE caught with no JS frame arrives at uncaughtException handler, kills host process, causes 92s gateway downtime with all in-flight sessions lost and mid-cron jobs orphaned. Attributed to Xsolla's NeuroNet production platform team. Root cause: stdin write to already-exited subprocess pipe. Workaround requires global uncaughtException filter.

signals.topic: Claude Opus 4.7 missing from hardcoded ACP model registry despite being generally available
signals.summary: The SDK's hardcoded model list (verified in SDK 0.2.131 cli.js) stops at claude-opus-4-6, excluding claude-opus-4-7 which has been GA on the Anthropic API, Claude Code CLI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Foundry since April 16, 2026. ACP consumers see the wrong model as latest.
aliases: claude-opus-4-7 not in ACP model list
signals.review_reason: Key model unavailable in SDK despite being GA everywhere else — users cannot use the latest Opus model via ACP. This directly blocks access to a generally available product feature. Evidence includes direct source grep confirmation in the published npm package (0.2.131).

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.7 missing from ACP model list (hardcoded model registry only includes up to Opus 4.6)
source_issues.evidence: SDK 0.2.131 npm package does not include claude-opus-4-7 in its hardcoded model registry, confirmed by grep of bundled cli.js. Model is GA across all other Anthropic platforms (API, CLI, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) since April 16, 2026. ACP users on Zed Industries' claude-agent-acp@0.23.1 are blocked from accessing the latest model.

signals.topic: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude instead of resolving plugin-loaded agent names
signals.summary: When a user passes a plugin-loaded agent name (e.g. 'my-plugin:test-agent') via the SDK's `Options.agent`, the SDK silently falls back to default Claude without any error, warning, or log line. The CLI's `--agent` flag handles the same name correctly. This is a silent failure mode that produces wrong agent behavior with no signal to the consumer.
aliases: plugin agent name not resolved in SDK
signals.review_reason: Silent failure that produces wrong behavior with no error signal. Users relying on plugin-loaded agents via the SDK get default Claude instead, potentially leading to wrong model responses, security implications (wrong agent context), and wasted API costs. The JSDoc explicitly promises equivalence with --agent which is violated.

source_issues.title: Options.agent silently falls back to default Claude for plugin-loaded agent names
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows SDK returns 'I'm Claude, an AI assistant…' (default) vs CLI returning 'I am TEST-AGENT-SMITH.' for the identical plugin agent name. JSDoc on Options.agent explicitly states 'This is equivalent to the --agent CLI flag' which is demonstrably false. No error, warning, or log line is emitted for the silent fallback. The only workaround requires re-declaring the agent inline via agents:.

signals.topic: Slash command XML wrapper persists verbatim in session transcript and leaks through session resume
signals.summary: When a user invokes a slash command (e.g. /context) via query(), the SDK persists the input as raw XML envelope (<command-name>, <command-message>, <command-args>) in the session JSONL transcript. On resume (via query({resume}) or getSessionMessages()), this XML is returned as the user message text — exposing internal serialization to consumers and feeding raw XML back into the model on subsequent turns.
aliases: slash command XML leaks in transcript
signals.review_reason: Data corruption of session history with downstream model contamination: raw XML is fed back into the LLM on subsequent turns. Chat UIs that display session history after resume show raw XML to users. This affects every SDK consumer who uses slash commands and session resume together.

source_issues.title: Slash command XML wrapper persists in session transcript and leaks through resumed history
source_issues.evidence: Every SDK consumer exposing slash commands with session resume hits this. Chat UIs display raw XML tags after page reload. If a consumer forks or appends to this turn, the wrapper XML is fed back to the model as tag soup it cannot meaningfully act on. Reporter provides working unwrapSlashCommandWrapper() workaround at their normalization layer. Impact confirmed as affecting the Express+WebSocket consumer's core resume flow.

signals.topic: query() with outputFormat json_schema crashes with internal null dereference (Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel'))
signals.summary: Using query() with a minimal outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: { type: 'object' } } crashes the SDK internally with a TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel'). This is a null dereference in the SDK's internal effort-resolution path (UT2() returns null) propagated to the request as taskIntensityOverride. The error surfaces as error_during_execution subtype with a misleading internal stack trace.
signals.review_reason: Structured output is a key SDK feature used for production integrations. A deterministic internal null dereference crashes the feature entirely with a misleading error message. Users cannot use json_schema structured output reliably. The error message is an internal SDK bug, not a user configuration issue.

source_issues.title: `query()` with minimal `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema" }` can crash internally with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'effortLevel')`
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic crash reproduced with 25-line minimal repro script. Internal null dereference in SDK code (UT2() returns null, read as .effortLevel). Checked across multiple SDK versions suggesting longstanding latent bug. Error surfaces as error_during_execution result subtype, making structured output usage unreliable. Workaround: caller must inspect result.errors field for misleading internal error.

signals.topic: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with end_turn and never invokes Bash, leaving multi-step workflows incomplete
signals.summary: Agent voluntarily halts after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason end_turn, never invoking Bash. Multi-step workflows fail to complete.

source_issues.title: Agent halts after Edit/Write phase with stop_reason: end_turn, never invokes Bash; multi-step prompts fail to complete (claude-sonnet-4-6)
source_issues.evidence: Agent reads files, makes Edits/Writes, then voluntarily halts with stop_reason: end_turn and empty result — never invoking Bash for verification, git ops, or gh pr create. Reproducible across seven runs in ~14 hours. TodoWrite items for unfinished steps are left in pending. 0 Bash invocations vs 42 in the working baseline.

signals.topic: claude install exits 0 but binary is not placed at expected path, causing downstream ENOENT crashes
signals.summary: Install script reports success but binary is missing, causing immediate ENOENT crash on next step.

This is a silent failure mode where the action looks like it completed normally but actually failed catastrophically. Related issue #1254 shows this is a recurring pattern.

source_issues.title: plugin_marketplaces fails: claude install exits 0 but binary not placed at ~/.local/bin/claude
source_issues.evidence: claude install emits warnings 'directory /home/runner/.local/bin does not exist' and 'claude command not found' yet exits 0 with '✔ Claude Code successfully installed!'. Next step (adding marketplace) immediately crashes with ENOENT: posix_spawn '/home/runner/.local/bin/claude'. Same action SHA and runner image worked 3 hours prior.

signals.topic: Action uses GitHub App credentials instead of workflow GITHUB_TOKEN, bypassing workflow permissions block and pushing commits when only review was requested

source_issues.title: claude-code-action pushes commits when only review was requested; workflow permissions: contents: read does not constrain it
source_issues.evidence: Workflow YAML declares 'permissions: contents: read' but action still pushed commits using GitHub App installation token instead of workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN.
