signals.topic: SDK sends anthropic_beta in request body but Bedrock only accepts it as HTTP header, causing 400 error on first API call
signals.summary: v1.0.113 breaks AWS Bedrock by sending beta flags in request body instead of HTTP header, causing immediate 400 error.
signals.review_reason: Breaking regression for AWS Bedrock users: v1.0.113 completely breaks Bedrock integration, causing immediate 400 error on first API call. Users must pin to v1.0.112 as workaround. This affects all Bedrock users who updated to the latest version.

source_issues.title: [BUG] v1.0.113 breaks AWS Bedrock: claude-agent-sdk@0.2.129 sends anthropic_beta in request body, causing 400 invalid beta flag
source_issues.evidence: v1.0.113 bumped SDK to 0.2.129 which sends beta flags in request body (anthropic_beta field). Bedrock only accepts them as HTTP header (anthropic-beta). Any body value causes 400 error. Fails on very first API call (num_turns: 1, duration_ms: 1226, input_tokens: 0). CLI flags like CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1 have no effect on SDK's internal HTTP transport.

signals.topic: Stale prompt files in RUNNER_TEMP leak between jobs on non-ephemeral self-hosted runners, causing cross-job context contamination
signals.summary: Prompt files from one job leak into unrelated jobs on self-hosted runners due to RUNNER_TEMP not being cleared.
signals.review_reason: Data leakage between jobs: a file from one job's context is incorporated into another unrelated job's model context on self-hosted runners. This causes the model to respond to stale requests from a different repository, creating incorrect and potentially confusing behavior.

source_issues.title: Stale prompt files in ${RUNNER_TEMP}/claude-prompts/ leak between jobs on non-ephemeral self-hosted runners
source_issues.evidence: claude-user-request.txt from a mention-mode invocation in repo A was repeatedly picked up by review invocations in repo B running on the same runner agent. Model addressed stale questions in PR review comments. Observed on 5 of 12 review jobs (~40% manifest rate) over 5 days. GitHub documentation claims RUNNER_TEMP is emptied between jobs but this is not honored on self-hosted runners.

signals.topic: False-positive filter silently fails due to deprecated Haiku model, causing PR comment spam and CI cost inflation
signals.summary: The false-positive filter in claude-code-security-review calls the deprecated model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022', which returns 404 and silently disables FP filtering. Every raw security finding is posted as a PR comment without noise suppression, flooding PRs with false positives and inflating CI costs.
aliases: deprecated Haiku model breaks FP filter
signals.review_reason: This is a functional regression in the core FP-filtering capability of the security-review action. The deprecated model causes silent failure (404 on every filter call), resulting in unfiltered findings flooding PR comments and unnecessary CI token consumption. The issue provides explicit logs and a clear user impact chain: deprecated model → 404 → filter disabled → all raw findings posted as comments. Only one occurrence in this dataset, but the impact is concrete and well-evidenced (not merely a security keyword match). Count=1 reflects actual data; priority P2 because it's a single-occurrence non-blocking regression.

source_issues.title: False-positive filter fails with 404: model 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' not found
source_issues.evidence: The false-positive filter step calls the deprecated Haiku model, receives a 404, and silently disables FP filtering. The main scan completes but every raw finding is posted as a PR comment with no noise filtering. Logs show: 'model: claude-3-5-haiku-20241022' returning not_found_error. This directly impacts users: PRs receive unfiltered false positive comments, increasing CI cost and review noise.

signals.topic: Account repeatedly demoted from paid to free, forcing re-payment and losing project data
signals.summary: Paid account users are repeatedly kicked to free tier without warning, requiring re-payment to restore access and losing projects and data each time.
signals.review_reason: Clear billing/permission failure causing account access loss and data unavailability. User is forced to repeatedly re-pay to recover their own paid-tier content. This is a severe subscription management bug despite the 'invalid' label (which refers to incomplete bug report form, not absence of impact).

source_issues.title: [BUG]
source_issues.evidence: User has paid multiple times on 2 cards; repeatedly demoted to free tier; had to pay again to recover data and projects. Platform: Claude Desktop (macOS).

signals.topic: Team plan organization plugin marketplace fails to sync with 'Authentication with GitHub failed' error
signals.summary: Organization admins cannot re-sync internal plugin marketplace; every attempt returns a GitHub authentication error even after reinstalling the GitHub connector.
aliases: team plan internal plugins not loading
signals.review_reason: Organization-level plugin access is blocked, preventing an entire team from using internal tooling. Repeated sync failures after multiple remediation attempts demonstrate persistent breakage rather than transient issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Organization Plugins Not Syncing (Failed to trigger sync.)
source_issues.evidence: Claude Team plan organization plugin marketplace fails to sync with 'Authentication with GitHub failed. Check that the Claude GitHub App is installed on this repository.' error. All troubleshooting attempted including GitHub App reinstall, connector reconnect, plugin removal/re-add. Issue persists across multiple sync attempts.

signals.topic: CCD auto-deletes session git worktrees mid-session, abruptly terminating remote control sessions and suspending live workflows
signals.summary: Claude Code Desktop auto-cleans per-session git worktrees without warning or grace period, killing active sessions and breaking remote control workflows for users managing live systems.
aliases: CCD worktree cleanup remote session kill
signals.review_reason: Hard workflow break with zero warning or grace period. Session is terminated mid-operation, remote control connection drops immediately, live systems (algorithmic trading, ops, on-call) are left suspended with no ability to reconnect remotely. Multiple occurrences in a single session. This is a P0 main-flow blocking issue despite count=1, because the user impact is severe (session termination of live systems with no recovery path).

source_issues.title: CCD auto-cleans session worktrees mid-work - breaks remote control workflow
source_issues.evidence: CCD spawns sessions in per-session git worktrees. Automatic cleanup (triggered post-PR-merge or idle) terminates sessions abruptly mid-work. Remote control connection drops instantly. User loses session without warning. Live system (algorithmic trading) left in suspended state. Happened twice in one session on 2026-05-06. No --no-worktree flag or grace period available.

signals.topic: Interactive TUI mode fails to spawn stdio MCP servers from project-scope .mcp.json, while headless mode works correctly
signals.summary: MCP servers configured in project .mcp.json with alwaysLoad:true are not spawned in interactive TUI mode, despite working in claude -p headless mode and claude mcp list health check.
aliases: MCP server project scope interactive mode not spawning
stdio MCP servers not loaded project config
mcp json project scope broken interactive TUI
signals.review_reason: Core MCP server loading is broken in the most commonly used interactive mode. The same configuration works in headless mode and health checks, making this an unambiguous regression. Users relying on project-scope MCP configs lose all MCP tool access in interactive TUI.

source_issues.title: Interactive mode does not spawn stdio MCP servers from project-scope .mcp.json (v2.1.131)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed behavior matrix: claude mcp list = works, claude -p headless = works, claude interactive TUI = broken. Tools not in ToolSearch registry in interactive mode. Workaround requires moving config from project-scope to user-scope.

signals.topic: /compact hangs remote client showing partial results until desktop-side input is received, blocking iOS/cowork usage
signals.summary: When /compact is run on a remote Claude Code session, the remote client (iOS/IDE) stops updating and displays partial results until input is provided on the host desktop, making remote/cowork usage impractical.
signals.review_reason: Core remote usage workflow is blocked. The remote client (iOS, IDE) becomes unusable until physical desktop input is provided, defeating the purpose of remote/cowork access. Multi-platform impact (iOS, IntelliJ, GoLand).

source_issues.title: [Bug] Compact command hangs remote client with partial results until desktop input received
source_issues.evidence: /compact claude remote to claude ios stops updating and shows partial results. Connection freezes until input on the remote server desktop is received. Affects IntelliJ and GoLand IDE remote clients, and iOS remote usage. Blocks the core remote/cowork use case.

signals.topic: hookify: Write tool silently bypasses event:file security rules — block action ineffective
signals.summary: Rules with `event: file` and `action: block` never fire for the Write tool because `rule_engine.py` reads `tool_input.get('new_string', '')` but Write sends `content` key. Security guardrails (credential detection, registry-pinning, content policy) provide zero enforcement when Claude uses Write instead of Edit.
aliases: event:file rules ineffective for Write tool
signals.review_reason: Security enforcement bypass with confirmed root cause. Rules explicitly set to `action: block` silently fail to fire for Write operations, leaving credential-detection and content-policy guardrails entirely ineffective. Users relying on hookify for security enforcement are unprotected in a non-obvious, silent way.

source_issues.title: hookify: Write tool silently bypasses event:file rules (action:block ineffective)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction: block rule matching 'pypi\.org' fires for Edit tool but silently passes through for Write tool. Security guardrails for credential detection and content policy enforcement are unprotected when Write is used.

signals.topic: fakechat: MCP server orphans after Claude Code abnormal exit — port 8787 held, reconnection fails
signals.summary: The fakechat `server.ts` (bun) does not self-terminate when parent Claude Code crashes or is killed. The orphaned bun holds port 8787 (FAKECHAT_PORT). Subsequent Claude Code sessions spawn a new MCP subprocess which fails with `EADDRINUSE`, causing `Failed to reconnect to plugin:fakechat:fakechat`.
signals.review_reason: Orphaned process holds a port required for reconnection, making the fakechat plugin unusable after any abnormal Claude Code termination. The reconnection failure is silent and non-obvious — users see a 'failed to reconnect' error without understanding the cause is a zombie bun process from a prior session.

source_issues.title: fakechat MCP server can outlive Claude Code and orphan-hold its port
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproduction: force-kill Claude Code process, `lsof -nP -i :8787` shows bun still listening with PPID=1. Next session fails with `EADDRINUSE` and `Failed to reconnect to plugin:fakechat:fakechat`.

signals.topic: telegram: Orphaned bun server saturates one CPU core indefinitely after parent session dies
signals.summary: The telegram `server.ts` (bun) can pin one CPU core at 100% for 42+ minutes after the parent Claude Code session dies abnormally. Root cause: uncaught EPIPE error in `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` handlers when stderr pipe breaks, causing a tight synchronous recursion that wedges the JS event loop. All three existing zombie-prevention mechanisms fail silently because the event loop is saturated.
signals.review_reason: Orphaned process causes sustained CPU saturation (one full core at 100% for 42+ minutes observed), representing a clear resource leak and performance degradation. The process survives and defeats all three independent cleanup mechanisms by wedging the JS event loop via an EPIPE recursion.

source_issues.title: [telegram] Orphaned bun server.ts can saturate one CPU core indefinitely after parent session dies
source_issues.evidence: Real-world observation: orphaned bun pegged one CPU core at 97.5% for 42+ minutes on macOS. Three existing safeguards (new-session takeover, orphan-PPID watchdog, 2-second hard exit) all failed silently because the event loop was synchronously saturated by EPIPE recursion.

signals.topic: typescript-lsp: LSP server fails to spawn on Windows (ENOENT) — plugin dead on arrival
signals.summary: On Windows, npm installs `typescript-language-server` as `.cmd`/`.ps1` shims with no `.exe`. The plugin hardcodes the bare command name. libuv's `spawn` on Windows does not resolve PATHEXT for non-.exe files without `shell: true`, so `uv_spawn('typescript-language-server')` returns ENOENT. `/doctor` reports the error and the LSP server never starts, making the plugin entirely non-functional on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Plugin is entirely non-functional on Windows due to spawn failure — ENOENT from libuv not resolving .cmd shims. Users on Windows get a dead plugin with no LSP support from typescript-lsp. Core functionality completely blocked.

source_issues.title: typescript-lsp: ENOENT on Windows — libuv can't spawn typescript-language-server (.cmd shim, no .exe)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: /doctor reports '✘ Plugin errors: ENOENT: no such file or directory, uv_spawn typescript-language-server' on Windows 11. npm installs only .cmd/.ps1 shims; no .exe exists. Plugin is non-functional.

signals.topic: telegram: SIGTERM-on-startup race kills sibling Claude sessions sharing bot token
signals.summary: Telegram `server.ts` sends SIGTERM to any PID found in `bot.pid` on startup to clean up crashed orphans. The PID file cannot distinguish a crashed orphan from an active sibling session. When a child session loads the same bot token, it SIGTERMs the parent listener's bun process, causing 'MCP server disconnected'. The symptom is intermittent disconnection mid-conversation in the standard Channels listener + per-message child session flow.
signals.review_reason: Siblings sessions using the standard telegram channel architecture are killed during startup, causing intermittent MCP disconnection mid-conversation. This is not an exotic setup — it is the documented default flow. The race condition is confirmed in real-world usage.

source_issues.title: SIGTERM-on-startup race kills sibling Claude sessions sharing the same bot token
source_issues.evidence: Real-world reproduction: observed twice in one session on Windows 11 with telegram plugin v0.0.6. Standard flow (Channels listener spawning per-message child sessions) triggers the race. Child session SIGTERMs parent listener, causing 'MCP server disconnected' mid-conversation.

signals.topic: Tutorial examples reference retired/deprecated Claude Haiku model, causing confusion and failed learning attempts
signals.summary: The tutorial's code examples use Claude Haiku 3, which has been recently retired. Users following the tutorial will encounter errors and failures when trying to reproduce the examples, as the referenced model version is no longer available.
aliases: Outdated model references in tutorial examples
signals.review_reason: The tutorial references a recently retired model (Haiku 3), meaning users who follow the tutorial will encounter API errors when running the code examples. This is a direct user-blocking issue for the interactive learning flow — users cannot successfully complete the tutorial as written. While count=1 and single-repo, the nature of a 'tutorial' implies potentially many users affected, and the problem is clearly demonstrated with a concrete issue report.

source_issues.title: Tutorial using Haiku 3- needs update
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports the tutorial still uses 'recently-retired Claude Haiku 3' and needs updating to Haiku 4.5, indicating the learning flow is broken for users following the current tutorial.

signals.topic: Plugin loader installs all repo skills instead of only marketplace.json-declared ones, causing duplicate skills and token waste
signals.summary: When installing document-skills or example-skills plugins, the loader installs all 17 skills from the repository instead of filtering by the `skills` array in marketplace.json. Installing both plugins results in duplicate skills, wasting ~50k tokens of context space.
aliases: plugin installs all skills instead of declared subset
signals.review_reason: 用户实际受影响：安装插件后出现17个重复技能定义，浪费约50k上下文token，减少了用于实际工作的可用上下文。虽为单仓问题，但影响明确（token浪费、重复加载），且issue #1087和issue #189均独立报告了同一根因的不同表现，有2条独立证据支撑。归为P2而非P0因count=2且为单仓问题，无多仓传播证据。

source_issues.title: document-skills plugin loads all skills from repo instead of only declared ones in marketplace.json
source_issues.evidence: Plugin installs 17 skills instead of the 4 declared in marketplace.json. Root cause: plugin loader loads all skill directories in source path without filtering against the `skills` array from marketplace.json. Cache contains all 17 skill folders.

source_issues.title: document-skills and example-skills plugins install identical content, causing duplicate skills
source_issues.evidence: Installing both plugins results in all 17 skills being installed identically under both plugin namespaces. ~50k wasted tokens from duplicate skill definitions. Skills like pptx (6.3k tokens) appear twice in /context. Both plugins use the same commit hash in cache.

signals.topic: eval-viewer generate_review.py cannot find eval_metadata.json at SKILL.md-specified location, rendering every run as '(No prompt found)'
signals.summary: The eval-viewer's generate_review.py walks the wrong directory depth for eval_metadata.json, missing files placed per SKILL.md instructions. This causes the viewer to show '(No prompt found)' for every eval run, breaking the review workflow for skill-creator users.
aliases: generate_review.py no prompt found for all runs
signals.review_reason: eval-viewer是skill-creator工具链的核心组成部分，其generate_review.py每次运行都将所有eval标记为'(No prompt found)'，直接阻断skill-creator用户的eval review工作流。用户提供了清晰的重现步骤和root cause定位（代码路径深度不匹配），且aggregate_benchmark.py（同一工具链）可正确读取该文件，说明这不是用户的配置错误而是工具bug。虽有workaround但属于体验严重降级，标记为P1因count=1且单仓，未达P0门槛。

source_issues.title: skill-creator: eval-viewer doesn't find per-eval metadata
source_issues.evidence: aggregate_benchmark.py reads eval_metadata.json at eval_dir/eval_metadata.json (correct per SKILL.md), but generate_review.py only checks run_dir/eval_metadata.json and run_dir.parent/eval_metadata.json, never reaching run_dir.parent.parent where the file actually lives. Repros: create workspace per SKILL.md, run aggregate_benchmark.py (succeeds), then run generate_review.py (every run shows '(No prompt found)'). Workaround exists: manually copy eval_metadata.json into each run-1/ directory. Environment: Claude Code with skill-creator on Termux/Android.

signals.topic: Queued message Send button silently deletes user input without adding to conversation history
signals.summary: When Goose is processing a task and user queues a message then clicks Send, the message is removed from the queue but never added to the conversation — user input is silently lost with no memory of it.
signals.review_reason: Two independent users report 100% reproducible silent data loss: queued messages are removed on Send click but never delivered to conversation. This is a main-flow UX bug causing user input to be silently discarded — not a cosmetic or edge-case issue. Both reports confirm the interrupt behavior fires correctly (task stops) but the message payload is dropped. High user impact: message is gone and user must manually retype.

source_issues.title: Queued message lost when clicking Send — message removed from queue but never added to conversation history
source_issues.evidence: Clicking Send on queued message stops task but message never appears in conversation history. Goose has no memory of it. User must retype. Described as 'destructive — it deletes user input without processing it.' Affects Desktop UI v1.33.1 with Databricks goose-claude-4-6-opus.

source_issues.title: Queued message interrupt kills processing and deletes the queued message
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible: clicking Send icon on queued message to interject causes Goose to stop processing AND delete the queued message — it never gets sent. 'This is 100% reproducible. It happens every single time.' Persists after full macOS reinstall + fresh Goose install.

signals.topic: DeepSeek thinking mode causes 400 errors on follow-up turns via OpenAI-compatible providers
signals.summary: DeepSeek models activate thinking mode by default, returning reasoning_content in responses. Goose's backend does not handle this field, causing a 400 error on subsequent turns, making multi-turn DeepSeek conversations unusable.
signals.review_reason: DeepSeek models are completely broken for multi-turn conversations when accessed via OpenAI-compatible providers. Root cause is clearly identified (reasoning_content field not handled) and the bug is reproducible. Users get a 400 error on every follow-up turn, which blocks the core chat interaction with DeepSeek models. Workaround exists but only for users who know about it.

source_issues.title: DeepSeek models via OpenAI-compatible providers fail: reasoning_content not handled
source_issues.evidence: Root cause clearly identified: DeepSeek API returns reasoning_content which Goose does not pass back in subsequent requests, causing 400 error. First turn works but follow-up messages fail with 'Bad request (400): Error from provider (DeepSeek): The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.' Workaround: use non-DeepSeek models. Affects OpenCode Go provider with deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro.

signals.topic: MCP elicitation responses not delivered to MCP server, causing Goose Desktop to hang indefinitely
signals.summary: When users respond to MCP elicitation prompts in Goose Desktop, the response is not successfully delivered to the MCP server, causing Goose Desktop to hang forever with no recovery. Related race condition causes same MCP server to be spawned multiple times.
signals.review_reason: MCP elicitation delivery failure causes Goose Desktop to hang indefinitely — a complete main-flow block for any session using MCP servers that emit elicitation requests. User cannot continue their session after submitting an elicitation response. This is not a cosmetic issue; the app becomes unresponsive with no recovery path. Screen recordings provide clear evidence of the hang.

source_issues.title: Race condition while connecting to MCP servers & elicitation errors
source_issues.evidence: Two bugs: (1) Race condition spawns same MCP server 3 times. (2) After users respond to elicitation, result is not delivered to MCP server and Goose Desktop hangs forever. Screen recordings attached showing the hang. LLM is still responsive but Goose is stuck. Affects macOS Desktop UI v1.33.1 with Google Gemini models.

signals.topic: Streamable HTTP MCP calls on Linux reset after ~30s despite higher configured timeout
signals.summary: On Linux, long-running Streamable HTTP MCP tool calls fail at ~30s because reqwest's default Linux TCP_USER_TIMEOUT (30s) fires before Goose's configured extension timeout. Users cannot run MCP tools that legitimately take longer than 30s.
signals.review_reason: Long-running MCP tool calls fail silently on Linux at 30s regardless of user-configured timeout. This blocks users from running legitimate MCP tools that require more than 30s (e.g., Elastic Agent Builder tools). Root cause is identified in reqwest TCP_USER_TIMEOUT default. High impact for Linux users relying on extended-timeout MCP integrations.

source_issues.title: Streamable HTTP MCP calls on Linux may reset after ~30s despite larger extension timeout
source_issues.evidence: Root cause: reqwest default TCP_USER_TIMEOUT is 30s on Linux and Goose does not override it when building Streamable HTTP client. Even with timeout: 300 configured, connection resets at ~30s. Affects legitimate long-running MCP tools like Elastic Agent Builder. Specific Rust code location identified in extension_manager.rs.

signals.topic: Default max_output_tokens=4096 silently truncates responses for local/OOV models, breaking complex tasks
signals.summary: When using local inference providers or models not in Goose's known list, max_tokens defaults to 4096, which is sent to the API and truncates responses. Users see the model stop mid-task with no indication of why.
aliases: max_tokens too low for local models
signals.review_reason: Default token limit of 4096 silently breaks complex tasks for local model users — the model stops mid-generation with no error message, making it appear Goose barely works. This is a deceptive failure mode: no error is shown, the user just gets incomplete output. Workaround requires manual config file editing, which average users won't discover. Clear cost: users cannot complete the tasks they came to use.

source_issues.title: Default max_output_tokens of 4096 is unreasonably low
source_issues.evidence: Local providers (llama_swap, lmstudio) with models not in known list default to 4096 max_tokens, causing responses to be silently truncated. 'The model keeps stopping in the middle of trying to do things, with no indication of why.' User had to manually set GOOSE_MAX_TOKENS after figuring out the root cause. Affects Apple Silicon Mac OS UI with Qwen variants.

signals.topic: Sign-up form missing phone number country code selector, blocking account registration
signals.summary: 用户在注册 Browserbase 时，表单缺少手机号国家区号选择器，导致部分用户（尤其是美国以外的用户）无法完成注册流程，只能通过邮件或 Slack 联系人工客服绕过。
aliases: phone number country code missing in signup form
cannot sign up without country code
signals.review_reason: 主注册流程被阻断，用户无法通过正常表单完成注册，需人工介入才能解决，属于明确的用户体验问题。虽然 count=1，但属于主流程阻断级别，标记为 P1 而非 P0。

source_issues.title: unable to sign up for Browserbase: missing phone number country code
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确报告在注册时因表单缺少国家区号字段，无法完成注册；提供的临时解法是通过邮件/Slack 联系客服手动创建账户，说明主流程被阻断。

signals.topic: 创建新会话时触发 404 错误（数据库写入竞态条件）
signals.summary: 用户点击 New Chat 创建新 thread 时，后端在 thread 信息写入数据库之前就尝试读取，导致前端先收到 404 错误后才正常显示。这是明确的时序竞态问题，用户体验受损。
signals.review_reason: 404 错误虽短暂但会显示给用户，是明确的 API 调用失败，属工作流运行时阻断（非主流程崩溃但影响新会话创建体验），有明确日志和截图证据。

source_issues.title: [bug]New chat的时候会先报一个404错误 然后才正常显示
source_issues.evidence: 创建新 thread 时连续返回 404 的两个 API 调用（runs 和 history），截图可见错误弹框；用户明确指出是 thread 信息未写入数据库就开始读取的竞态条件

signals.topic: 文件输出触发两次流式渲染
signals.summary: AI 第一次写入文件时流式展示正常，但文件被复制到输出目录时再次触发了一次流式写入，导致同一内容显示两次。
signals.review_reason: 文件内容重复展示属于明显的体验下降，用户可见的输出错误，但影响范围限于文件输出场景，非高频路径。

source_issues.title: 一个文件输出会经历两次流式输出展示
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确描述：第一次写入文件后进行一次流式输出，文件复制到输出目录时又触发了一次相同的流式输出写入

signals.topic: 上下文压缩过于频繁且将内部压缩消息暴露给用户
signals.summary: 几乎每次 LLM 调用都触发上下文压缩，且压缩过程的内部消息被直接展示在对话界面，用户无法区分正常对话内容和系统内部操作。
signals.review_reason: 内部系统消息暴露给用户是明确的体验下降，高频触发（每次 LLM 调用）严重影响对话连贯性，有截图证据支撑。

source_issues.title: 压缩上下文过于频繁且作为内容进行输出
source_issues.evidence: 用户截图显示对话界面中出现了压缩相关消息；用户明确指出'基本每次llm调用都会进行一次上下文压缩'

signals.topic: 升级多用户版本后历史聊天记录和记忆数据丢失
signals.summary: 用户升级到支持多用户的版本后，无法再看到原有的聊天历史和记忆数据，后端文件（threads 和 memory.json）仍然存在，但用户无法通过界面访问。
aliases: lost chat history after multi-user update
signals.review_reason: 用户数据不可访问是严重的服务质量问题，升级路径缺少数据迁移机制导致历史数据丢失，用户有明确的数据存在证据（文件仍存）。

source_issues.title: lost chat history and memory after updating
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确说明升级多用户支持后原有聊天历史和记忆消失，后端文件仍存在于 .deerflow/threads 和 memory.json，但界面无法访问

signals.topic: AI 首条用户消息被自动改写为摘要内容
signals.summary: 当用户选择 AI 的改进意见并发送时，AI 会将用户的第一条消息改写为以'Here is a summary of the conversation to date:'开头的摘要，且在后续对话中持续修改该摘要。这是用户输入被框架篡改，用户感知明确且不可接受。
signals.review_reason: 用户输入被框架自动改写是严重的数据完整性问题，直接影响对话的原始性和可追溯性，用户明确表达了不满和质疑。

source_issues.title: 对话的第一条消息会被修改
source_issues.evidence: 用户明确描述 AI 在生成改进意见后，用户的首条消息被改为摘要内容，且随着对话继续不断被修改；用户质疑'直接篡改用户提问是否合理'

signals.topic: Cline sends unsupported `temperature` parameter causing API failures across multiple providers/models
signals.summary: Cline sends a deprecated or invalid `temperature` parameter to various API providers (Amazon Bedrock for Opus 4.7, Moonshot Kimi K2.6 via OpenAI Compatible), causing HTTP 400 errors that block the main coding workflow entirely.
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：3条issue均因Cline发送provider不支持的temperature参数导致API调用失败（HTTP 400），用户无法使用Bedrock Opus 4.7和Moonshot Kimi K2.6进行任何编码任务。三条issue指向同一根因（temperature参数未针对provider/model做适配），属于典型的高频+阻断组合。

source_issues.title: Error using Claude Opus 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock: `temperature` is deprecated
source_issues.evidence: User tries to use Opus 4.7 on Bedrock; API returns error: 'temperature` is deprecated for this model.' Main workflow blocked.

source_issues.title: Error using Claude Opus 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock: `temperature` is deprecated
source_issues.evidence: Same issue; closed with no resolution noted in this snapshot. Confirms it is a real user-impacting regression.

source_issues.title: Moonshot Kimi K2.6 fails via OpenAI Compatible because Cline sends unsupported temperature
source_issues.evidence: Kimi K2.6 via OpenAI Compatible fails with '400 invalid temperature: only 1 is allowed for this model.' API call blocked, similar root cause as Bedrock issue.

signals.topic: Windows-specific: deleting one MCP server causes all configured MCP servers to be removed
signals.summary: On Windows, removing a single MCP server from the Cline MCP server list causes all other configured MCP servers to be silently deleted. This is a data-loss bug that affects all MCP users on Windows.
aliases: Windows MCP server removal deletes all servers
signals.review_reason: 严重数据丢失缺陷：用户在Windows上删除一个MCP server后，所有配置的MCP servers全部消失。附有视频证据。虽然只有1条issue，但用户影响极其严重（所有MCP配置丢失），且明确为Windows特定回归bug，应标记为P1而非降级。

source_issues.title: [Windows Specific] Cline: Removing one MCP server deletes all configured MCP servers
source_issues.evidence: Video evidence provided showing that after removing one MCP server on Windows, all other MCP servers are gone. Confirmed by QA reporter. Critical data loss for MCP users.

signals.topic: Clicking 'New Task' after task completion reuses previous task context instead of starting fresh
signals.summary: After completing a task, clicking the 'New Task' button does not reset the task state. The previous task context is reused and gets triggered again, causing unexpected behavior and wasted AI tokens.
aliases: New Task button not resetting session
task state not cleared on new task
old task auto-restart on new task
signals.review_reason: 主流程体验破坏：点击'New Task'后系统未重置任务状态，复用了旧的上下文并重新触发上一任务。用户本意是开始新任务却发现旧任务被重新执行，造成混乱并浪费token。虽然只有1条issue，但属于SDK迁移引入的明确回归，症状清晰（有视频），P1合理。

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Previous task restarts automatically when clicking "New Task" after completion
source_issues.evidence: After completing a task, clicking 'New Task' reuses old task context and retriggers the previous task. QA reporter with video evidence. Old task data like {'hookName':'TaskCancel','status':'completed'} appears.

signals.topic: Unable to login to staging environment during Cline SDK migration
signals.summary: Users cannot log in to the staging environment when switching from production via the account section. The sign-up/sign-in flow navigates to the browser but the confirmation button fails, blocking the entire staging authentication path.
signals.review_reason: 阻断性认证问题：SDK迁移后staging环境登录流程断裂。用户通过account切换到staging后无法完成登录确认（有视频证据）。Staging环境是开发测试关键路径，此bug直接阻断该路径使用。

source_issues.title: [Cline SDK migration] Cline: Unable to login to staging environment
source_issues.evidence: QA reporter documents exact steps: switch to staging environment, click sign-up with cline, navigate to browser, click confirm — login fails. Video evidence attached. Blocks staging environment usage.

signals.topic: Account tab missing user name, email, and environment option after SDK migration upgrade
signals.summary: After upgrading to the latest build, the Cline Account tab does not display the user's name, email, or the Cline Environment selector, making it impossible to verify account identity or switch environments.
aliases: account details not displayed SDK upgrade
signals.review_reason: 关键信息缺失：Account tab在SDK升级后无法显示用户名、邮箱和环境选择器，用户无法验证身份或切换环境，属于主UI信息缺失。SDK迁移引入的明确回归，有截图证据支撑。

source_issues.title: Cline SDK migration: Account tab details missing after upgrading to latest build (Name, Email, Environment option not displayed)
source_issues.evidence: After latest build upgrade, Account tab shows blank for user name, email, and environment. QA reporter with screenshot evidence. Makes it impossible to verify account or switch between staging/production.

signals.topic: Chat mode displays 'Don't think' blocking message and refuses to respond, making Continue unusable for coding tasks
signals.summary: When users try to use chat mode (including /intent and /troubleshoot commands), Continue displays a 'Don't think for this request - Ask a question instead' message and refuses to provide any assistance. This blocks the primary interaction workflow, making the plugin effectively unusable for its core purpose.
aliases: Chat mode shows 'Ask a question' instead of responding
Intent command fails with blocking message
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：chat mode是Continue的核心交互方式，显示'Don't think'拒绝消息直接导致用户无法获得任何AI辅助，完全无法完成编码任务。用户明确描述'impossible to use Continue'，且issue活跃度高（10条评论），是明确的用户痛点而非功能请求。

source_issues.title: When I use /troubleshoot it tells me 'Don't think' and refuses to help
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'When I enter a prompt in chat mode, I don't receive a reply. Continue displays a message saying "Don't think for this request - Ask a question instead". This is making it impossible for me to use Continue, as I cannot get help with coding tasks.' Environment: Windows 11, Continue 0.9.195, VS Code 1.99.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet via OpenRouter. 10 comments on the issue indicates community relevance.

signals.topic: Inline edit fails on Vue dynamic route files with bracket filenames (e.g. [id].vue in Nuxt projects), making Continue unusable in such projects
signals.summary: Continue inline edit feature throws an error when editing Vue files that have brackets in their filenames, such as [id].vue used in Nuxt.js dynamic routes. This prevents the plugin from being used in Nuxt projects until the issue is resolved.
aliases: Inline edit fails on Nuxt dynamic route Vue files
Bracket characters in Vue filename cause edit error
Cannot edit [id].vue files in Nuxt projects
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：inline edit是Continue的核心功能之一，在Nuxt项目中处理包含方括号[]的文件名时直接报错，导致用户在Nuxt项目中完全无法使用Continue编辑功能。用户明确描述'plugin unusable in my project'，属于真实用户影响证据。count=1且仅单仓，但用户影响明确（阻断特定项目类型使用），保留为P2边缘改进项。

source_issues.title: Erreur on file [id].vue
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'I keep getting an error when modifying the [id].vue files in my Nuxt project because of the brackets []. The plugin is therefore unusable in my project until this issue is fixed.' Labels indicate kind:bug, area:inline-edit. The error is confirmed to be caused by bracket characters in filenames.

signals.topic: BrightData SERP tool generates broken search URLs due to JavaScript template literal syntax in Python f-strings
signals.summary: BrightDataSearchTool's get_search_url method uses `${query}` (JS template literal syntax) instead of `{query}` (Python f-string syntax), causing all search queries to be prepended with a literal `$` character. All three engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) are affected, making the entire search tool non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed functional bug: the BrightDataSearchTool is completely non-functional for all users due to JS `${}` syntax in Python f-strings. All three search engines (Google, Bing, Yandex) produce broken URLs. This is a direct, reproducible workflow failure affecting a core tool integration. The bug is in a shipped tool (brightdata_serp.py) and has clear reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: [BUG] BrightData SERP tool uses JavaScript template syntax in Python f-strings, breaking all search queries
source_issues.evidence: Every search query generates a URL like `https://www.google.com/search?q=$AI%20news` instead of `https://www.google.com/search?q=AI%20news`. The bug is in `brightdata_serp.py` lines 132-137. Reproduction steps provided with exact code. The tool is completely broken for all users of the BrightData search integration.

signals.topic: ConditionalTask with output_pydantic and guardrail causes TypeError, crashing crew execution
signals.summary: When a ConditionalTask references a context task with output_pydantic, and also has its own output_pydantic and guardrail, CrewAI internally calls json.loads() on a Pydantic object instead of its serialized JSON string, raising TypeError and crashing the entire crew execution.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed blocking bug: the combination of ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context causes a TypeError that crashes the entire crew execution. The error occurs in the internal serialization path where a Pydantic model object is passed to json.loads() instead of a string. Root cause is identified in the issue analysis. This blocks a real multi-task workflow pattern using Pydantic output models.

source_issues.title: [BUG] TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not <PydanticModel> when combining ConditionalTask + output_pydantic + guardrail + context
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash: using ConditionalTask with context from a task that has output_pydantic, combined with its own output_pydantic and guardrail, causes 'TypeError: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not DrugClassificationOutput'. Crew execution fails entirely. Root cause identified: Pydantic object from context task passed directly to json.loads() without .model_dump_json() call.

signals.topic: HITL pre-review silently fails without logging or exception, bypassing automated safeguards with no user signal
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(learn=True) is used and _pre_review_with_lessons encounters any exception (network, auth, LLM, structured-output), the implementation catches all exceptions and returns the original method_output silently. No exception is propagated, no warning is logged, and callers cannot distinguish pre-reviewed output from raw model output.
signals.review_reason: This is a silent degradation bug: the HITL pre-review layer silently fails on any exception (network, auth, LLM, structured-output) and returns raw output with no signal to callers. While not a hard crash, the automated safety layer (learn=True) can be silently bypassed with no logging, which violates the user's expectation of automated pre-review. The downstream system cannot distinguish safe pre-reviewed output from unvetted model output. This qualifies as experience degradation in a safety-critical code path.

source_issues.title: [BUG] HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: The except block in _pre_review_with_lessons (lib/crewai/src/crewai/flow/human_feedback.py) catches all exceptions and returns method_output without logging or propagating the exception. Downstream components receive raw output but cannot tell pre-review ran or failed. No warning or error is logged in this path. Users have no signal that automated safeguards were bypassed.

signals.topic: Opus-4.7 模型 temperature 参数已废弃，导致 API 调用直接返回 400 阻断主流程
signals.summary: 使用 Opus-4.7 模型时，fabric 发送的 `temperature` 参数已被 Anthropic API 废弃，导致每次请求均返回 400 Bad Request，用户无法完成任何 AI 对话，必须手动修复配置才能继续使用。
aliases: Claude Opus-4.7 temperature deprecated API error
temperature parameter deprecated for model causing 400 error
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断级别问题：每次使用 Opus-4.7 模型的 API 调用均失败，返回 400 错误，导致整个对话流程不可用，用户必须手动修复配置才能继续。这是明确的用户影响证据（主流程阻断）。虽然 count=1，但 400 错误为高频单次阻断，所有请求均失败，review_reason 已给出强用户影响证据（阻断主流程 + API 错误），符合 P0 条件。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Opus-4.7 temperature deprecated for this model
source_issues.evidence: API 返回 400 Bad Request: `temperature` is deprecated for this model；issue 被标记为 bug 且状态为 closed；用户 macOS Silicon + Homebrew 安装，受影响版本 v1.4.451；所有使用 Opus-4.7 的 API 调用均被阻断

signals.topic: 未指定 pattern 时 CLI 错误信息使用二进制名称作为 pattern 名，产生误导性错误阻止用户定位问题
signals.summary: 用户在不传递 `-p` 参数的情况下调用 `fabric-ai`（如 `fabric-ai update` 或 `fabric-ai -y URL --transcript`），CLI 回退到使用二进制名称 `fabric-ai` 作为 pattern 名进行查找，产生完全误导的错误信息 `pattern 'fabric-ai' not found`，导致用户误以为工具未安装或 Homebrew 配置损坏，而非意识到未指定 pattern；同时 README 中的 zsh yt() 示例也因此失效。
aliases: binary name used as pattern fallback misleading error
missing pattern flag produces confusing error message
README yt() shell helper broken after #1960
signals.review_reason: 用户体验显著下降：错误信息将用户引向完全错误的方向（工具未安装、Homebrew 问题），而非真正原因（未指定 pattern），且 README 中的官方 shell integration 示例因此失效。虽然不阻断基本功能（加 `-p` 仍可工作），但对于常见使用场景（YouTube transcript、类子命令调用）产生严重误导，count=1 单仓问题定性为 P2。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Misleading "pattern '<binary-name>' not found" when no pattern is specified, plus README zsh yt() example is broken since #1960
source_issues.evidence: v1.4.452 版本中，`fabric-ai -y URL --transcript` 和 `fabric-ai update` 均产生误导错误；受影响用户范围：所有不带 `-p` 参数使用 yt() helper 或类子命令式调用的用户；README 中的 zsh yt() 示例因此完全失效；错误信息指向完全错误的方向（工具未安装/包管理问题），而非真正的问题（未指定 pattern）。

signals.topic: Gemini CLI crashes with out-of-memory / heap overflow during file operations or idle time
signals.summary: Users experience fatal JavaScript heap OOM crashes — both during resource-intensive operations (processing ~1000 files) and while left idle — consuming up to 7.17 GB RAM before crashing. The same root cause (insufficient memory management) manifests in two distinct scenarios.
signals.review_reason: Two distinct crash reports (one idle, one during file ops) sharing the same OOM/heap exhaustion root cause. Both produce fatal crashes that fully block the user's session. count=2 in same repo; P1 rather than P0 per single-repo threshold, but high severity given fatal crash + GB-level memory consumption before failure.

source_issues.title: gemini crashed with OOM while idle
source_issues.evidence: Gemini detected 7.17 GB high memory usage, then crashed with JavaScript heap overflow (FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit). Also showed anomalous self-answering behavior and system prompt dumping.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI ran out of memory and crashed
source_issues.evidence: Requested ~1000 file list, resulted in FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory, with full Node.js GC logs showing progressive heap exhaustion.

signals.topic: Delete chat session fails with JSON SyntaxError, leaving orphaned session files
signals.summary: Deleting old chat sessions via CLI or TUI fails because the associated JSON session file is malformed (SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}'), preventing the session and its artifacts from being fully removed.
signals.review_reason: Clear user-blocking bug: the delete-session command (core user workflow) fails with a parse error, leaving orphaned files. No workaround available. Fully reproducible with a stack trace pointing to ChatRecordingService.deleteSessionAndArtifacts.

source_issues.title: unable to delete old chats / sessions.
source_issues.evidence: Error deleting associated file session-2026-04-23T07-50-51abad7e.json: SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1. The session is marked deleted but the file artifact remains, resulting in partial/failed cleanup.

signals.topic: CLI uses Linux shell commands on Windows due to platform detection failure
signals.summary: On Windows, Gemini CLI consistently uses Linux commands (e.g., bash-style) instead of Windows equivalents, making the tool functionally unusable for Windows users who expect cross-platform behavior.
signals.review_reason: Critical cross-platform breakage on Windows: the CLI defaults to Linux commands, making it unusable for the entire Windows user base. This blocks the primary use case (AI-assisted command execution) for an entire OS class.

source_issues.title: Gemini CLI does not get context of it's envrionment, it constantly uses linux commands on a windows machine
source_issues.evidence: User on win32 v25.9.0 reports CLI 'constantly uses linux commands on a windows machine'. Client info confirms OS: win32. The assistant fails to adapt to Windows environment, making core operations fail.

signals.topic: Reproducible CLI crash when executing shell commands via cargo check
signals.summary: On Alpine Linux aarch64 running in Lima VM on macOS, Gemini CLI reproducibly crashes when it attempts to execute a shell command (cargo check), hanging and requiring process termination. Marked as priority/p1 by project triagers.
signals.review_reason: Explicitly triaged as priority/p1 and kind/bug by project triage bots. Reproducible crash on shell execution — a core feature — blocks the primary workflow for affected users. No workaround available.

source_issues.title: Executing shell command crash
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible crash when executing shell command. CLI hangs at 'Shell cargo check' step then crashes. Marked priority/p1 by project triage. Multiple TERM settings tried without resolution.

signals.topic: CLI crashes with ENOENT error when pasting text containing dot-separated words
signals.summary: Pasting any text containing dot-separated words (e.g., class names like SoortContact.Contact) causes the CLI to crash with ENOENT: no such file or directory, because the text is incorrectly interpreted as a file path.
signals.review_reason: Everyday workflow blocker: any user pasting code (which commonly contains dot-separated identifiers like class names) experiences a crash with full stack trace. Frequent and disruptive. Workaround is to avoid pasting code, which defeats a primary use case.

source_issues.title: CLI crashes with ENOENT error when pasting text containing dot-separated words.
source_issues.evidence: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'SoortContact.Contact' — the CLI interprets dot-separated text as a file path and crashes. Full stack trace provided. User must avoid pasting any code with class/method names.

signals.topic: MCP tool calls logged as Python interpreter code instead of structured tool calls in agent memory
signals.summary: When using MCP tools with CodeAgent, tool calls are incorrectly logged as python_interpreter code blocks in agent.memory.get_full_steps(), making it impossible to retrieve structured MCP tool names and kwargs for end-to-end testing or audit trails. Users must resort to monkey-patching to extract this information.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point: MCP tool calls are logged as python_interpreter code strings instead of structured tool_call records in agent.memory, preventing programmatic introspection needed for end-to-end testing. The workaround (monkey-patching) confirms this is not an edge case — users need proper structured access to MCP tool invocations. Impact is clear: workflow blocked, not just a cosmetic issue. Count=1 keeps it at P1 rather than P0, as the issue is scoped to a specific use case (MCP + memory introspection) rather than general execution failure.

source_issues.title: BUG: MCP tools calls gets logged inside the Python Code interpreter
source_issues.evidence: User reports that iterating over agent.memory.get_full_steps() after a run with MCP tools shows python_interpreter code blocks containing MCP calls as string literals, rather than structured tool_call entries with name/kwargs. This breaks end-to-end testing workflows that depend on extracting tool calls programmatically. User had to monkey-patch the forward method of MCP tools as a workaround.

signals.topic: Codex model integration fails to maintain interactive session loop — agent stops prematurely
signals.summary: 用户在使用 Codex 模型运行 autoresearch 交互式会话时，Codex 忽略 'never stop' 指令导致会话提前终止，而 Claude 模型无此问题。40 条评论说明这是社区高关注的持续性问题。
signals.review_reason: 用户痛点明确：主流程阻断（Codex 交互式会话完全不可用），作者明确表示'Codex doesn't work'，40 条评论证明社区持续受影响。虽然 count=1，但用户影响证据充分（交互式会话核心功能对特定模型不可用），优先级定为 P1。

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告 Codex 完全无法与 autoresearch 配合使用，因其忽略 'never stop' 指令导致交互式会话提前终止。40 条评论表明社区对此问题持续讨论，作者明确表示更偏好交互式会话但因该 bug 无法使用。

signals.topic: FilesystemMiddleware READ_FILE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION uses wrong kwarg name (path vs file_path) — causes Pydantic validation failure on every file read
signals.summary: The READ_FILE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION constant shows three worked examples using `path=` as the kwarg name, but the actual tool schema declares the field as `file_path`. Models follow the description's dominant pattern and emit `read_file(path=...)`, causing Pydantic to reject the call with 'Field required: file_path'. Every file read attempt wastes at least one LLM turn for retry.
aliases: read_file kwarg mismatch description vs schema
Pydantic validation failure on read_file due to wrong kwarg in description
path vs file_path kwarg confusion in filesystem tool description
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降 + 成本损失：read_file 是 agent 最高频使用的工具之一，每次读取文件都因 kwarg 名称不匹配而触发 Pydantic 验证失败，强制重试一次 LLM 调用。两个独立外部用户报告了同一问题，说明影响面广且持续存在于每一次文件读取操作中。

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware: read_file description shows examples with wrong kwarg name (path vs schema's file_path)
source_issues.evidence: READ_FILE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION shows three worked-example call sites using path= but actual schema declares file_path. Models follow description examples and emit read_file(path=...) triggering Pydantic 'Field required: file_path'. This wastes a turn on retry every time the agent reads a file.

source_issues.title: FilesystemMiddleware: read_file description shows examples with wrong kwarg name (path vs schema's file_path)
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #3188: READ_FILE_TOOL_DESCRIPTION constant shows worked examples using path instead of file_path=. Schema correctly declares file_path but description teaches wrong kwarg. Models pick up dominant pattern and emit read_file(path=...) which fails validation.

signals.topic: execute tool hardcodes status='success' on non-zero exit code — causes infinite agent loops and massive token waste
signals.summary: The execute tool ToolMessage always returns status='success' even when the command exits with non-zero code, giving agents no signal to stop retrying. Production case shows 638 LLM turns / 8.8M tokens wasted on a single file-not-found error loop.
aliases: execute tool always returns success on command failure
non-zero exit code not reflected in ToolMessage status
agent spirals on failed execute calls
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：execute 是 agent 的核心工具，返回硬编码 success 导致 agent 无法感知命令失败，持续重试。在生产环境中造成 8.8M token 的直接经济损失，每一次失败的 execute 调用都会触发该问题。

source_issues.title: execute tool hardcodes status='success' on non-zero exit code
source_issues.evidence: Production deployment: FileNotFoundError on every execute call caused agent to spiral for 638 LLM turns / 8.8M tokens because status='success' gave no signal to stop retrying. LangSmith traces also show failed commands as 'success', making error filtering impossible for operators.

signals.topic: LocalShellBackend used by default in CLI — unsandboxed arbitrary shell execution on host system
signals.summary: deepagents-cli defaults to LocalShellBackend when sandbox=None, giving agents full unsandboxed access to the host OS including filesystem, network, and privilege escalation. Users running `deepagents-cli` locally with default settings are exposed.
aliases: CLI default sandbox=None leads to unsandboxed shell execution
LocalShellBackend enables host OS access by default
unsandboxed execute tool in CLI default config
signals.review_reason: 安全+体验双重阻断：CLI 默认配置使用 LocalShellBackend，用户在本地运行 deepagents-cli 时 agent 拥有宿主机的完全 shell 访问权限，等同于以当前用户权限无沙箱执行任意命令。影响所有使用默认配置运行 CLI 的用户，是严重的安全和系统完整性问题。

source_issues.title: Unsandboxed Code Execution via LocalShellBackend in CLI Agent
source_issues.evidence: When sandbox=None (default), LocalShellBackend provides an unsandboxed execute tool running commands directly on host OS. Root cause in libs/cli/deepagents_cli/agent.py: create_cli_agent() uses LocalShellBackend by default. Enables full filesystem access, network access, process spawning, and privilege escalation through the agent.

signals.topic: CLI fails on OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoints (LM Studio, Ollama, etc.) — blocks self-hosted / local model usage
signals.summary: The CLI defaults use_responses_api=true for OpenAI provider, but most OpenAI-compatible third-party services only support Chat Completions-style streaming, not the OpenAI Responses API event format. Users with local or self-hosted models get 'No generations found in stream' and cannot use the CLI at all.

signals.topic: langchain-deepseek: reasoning_content not passed back causes 400 error on multi-turn agent calls

signals.review_reason: Multi-turn agent conversations with DeepSeek models (deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-r1) are completely blocked by this bug. Appears across 4 unique issues (including 1 open), all confirmed with stack traces. Blocks any agentic workflow using DeepSeek thinking mode in multi-step conversations.

signals.topic: Checkpoint serialization bloat causes 85% storage overhead, 37.8% token overhead, and silent corrupt payload pass-through
signals.summary: LangGraph checkpoint serialization uses full Pydantic metadata via dumpd(), producing 6.79x storage bloat and silent acceptance of structurally corrupt payloads that reach the LLM unchanged. Projected $372K/year cost impact.
signals.review_reason: 虽count=1但提供了量化基准（85%存储开销、37.8% token开销）及$372,600/年的成本影响估算，属于明显成本损失。4类损坏载荷静默通过验证存在结构性安全问题，无任何opt-out路径，主流程代价持续叠加。

source_issues.title: LangGraph checkpoint serialization produces 85% storage bloat and 37.8% token overhead with no opt-out path
source_issues.evidence: Measured 85.3% storage overhead (21,850 vs 3,217 bytes for 16-turn ReAct), 37.8% token overhead, silent pass-through of 4 categories of corrupt payloads. Projected annual cost impact $372,600 at 10M loops/year. No pluggable serializer interface.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared metadata dict by reference, leaking thread_id between invocations
signals.summary: ensure_config assigns metadata key by reference without calling .copy(), causing configurable values like thread_id from one invocation to contaminate the base config shared across all future invocations.
signals.review_reason: 单仓问题但影响严重：跨会话状态泄露导致thread_id等配置数据污染，阻断多租户/多会话场景的正确性，属于关键功能不可用的会话状态类问题。10条评论说明持续关注度。

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: After first invocation with thread_id=X, subsequent invocations see base config metadata as {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent', 'thread_id': 'X'} — prior invocation data leaks into shared base config, contaminating all future calls in the same process. 10 comments confirm ongoing discussion.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud, causing 2-3x redundant work and cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls exceeding ~3 minutes are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while original is still running. Both complete successfully, causing 2-3x duplicate LLM calls and cost.
signals.review_reason: 云端运行时静默重复执行导致2-3倍成本浪费，属于关键功能不可用+明显成本损失。9条评论确认无workaround，跨版本持续存在，直接影响长时任务用户。主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate tool calls appear in LangSmith traces with identical arguments and no preceding model node. Affects deepagents SubAgentMiddleware with sub-agents taking 3-10 minutes. BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 is hardcoded. No workaround effective. 9 comments confirm persistence across versions 1.1.3-1.1.6.

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt/$gte/$lt/$lte) use lexicographic text comparison instead of numeric, producing silently wrong query results
signals.summary: PostgresStore._get_filter_condition uses value->>key (text extraction) with str(value) for numeric operators, causing PostgreSQL to compare numbers as text strings. '9' >= '10' evaluates True in text ordering, silently returning incorrect filtered results.
signals.review_reason: 数据库查询返回静默错误结果，是数据正确性类主流程失败。虽count=1但影响严重：用户信任过滤结果但实际返回错误数据，SqliteStore已有正确实现说明这是未完成的移植修复。

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: Filter {'score': {'$gte': 10}} incorrectly includes items with score=2..9 because '9' >= '10' is True in PostgreSQL text ordering. SqliteStore already handles this correctly with CAST(... AS REAL) but fix was not propagated to PostgresStore.

source_issues.title: langgraph dev falsely reports Port 2024 already in use due to TIME-WAIT entries
source_issues.evidence: After Ctrl+C to stop langgraph dev, restarting immediately raises OSError: Port 2024 is already in use. No process is LISTEN-ing. User must wait 60 seconds or reboot. Proposed fix uses SO_REUSEADDR.

signals.topic: Python: MCPStreamableHTTPTool raises CancelledError instead of proper exceptions when MCP server is unreachable, breaking user error handling
signals.summary: When an MCP server is unreachable, the framework's context manager cleanup raises asyncio.CancelledError which escapes the user's try-except block, making it impossible to handle connection failures gracefully. The same issue affects OpenAIChatCompletionClient.
aliases: CancelledError propagated from async context manager cleanup
signals.review_reason: Framework-level error handling broken: CancelledError from async context manager cleanup bypasses user try-except, making MCP connection failure unhandleable. This is a main flow failure for any production deployment relying on MCP tools — users cannot implement retry or graceful degradation.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Error Handling Issue regarding Python MCPStreamableHTTPTool Class
source_issues.evidence: User provides full reproduction code showing CancelledError escaping try-except block. Error trace: 'asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError: Cancelled via cancel scope' thrown from async context manager __aenter__, bypassing user exception handlers. Also explicitly notes OpenAIChatCompletionClient has same issue.

signals.topic: Python: require_script_approval=True fails with HTTP 400 'Expected toolResult blocks' for code-defined @script skills

signals.review_reason: Main flow blocked: the require_script_approval feature is entirely broken for code-defined scripts. Every user who tries to combine require_script_approval=True with @script-decorated skills gets a 400 error. This is not an edge case — it is the core use case of script approval gating failing.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: require_script_approval=True fails with 400 'Expected toolResult blocks' for code-defined (@script) skills

The workaround is to remove require_script_approval=True, which defeats the purpose of the feature.

source_issues.title: .NET: `externalLoop` + `ApprovalRequiredAIFunction` leaves dangling `function_call` in Azure Conversations API, breaks resume
