signals.review_reason: Critical feature (human-in-the-loop tool approval) is entirely non-functional in the hosted agent deployment scenario. The framework explicitly warns that the required content type is unsupported, making it impossible for users to implement approval-gated tool execution in production hosted deployments.

source_issues.title: Python: Hosted Agent Framework: human-in-the-loop tool approval not working
source_issues.evidence: User provides exact warning from logs: 'Content type function_approval_request is not supported yet. This is usually safe to ignore.' Combined with no usable response in playground. User explicitly states: 'hosted orchestration cannot yet support these approval steps end-to-end.' Questions roadmap/timeline.

signals.topic: UnicodeDecodeError in MagenticOne WebSurfer on non-English Windows environments
signals.summary: PlaywrightController reads page_script.js without specifying UTF-8 encoding, causing UnicodeDecodeError (cp950 codec) when the script contains non-ASCII characters and the system locale is non-English. This crashes MagenticOne WebSurfer on startup for non-English Windows users.
signals.review_reason: This is a real user-facing crash affecting the MagenticOne WebSurfer component on non-English Windows systems. The UnicodeDecodeError is reproducible and blocks the entire WebSurfer from initializing. While count=1, the evidence is exceptionally strong (full stack trace + minimal repro + fix) and the blocking nature (complete component failure on startup for non-English users) warrants P1.

source_issues.title: open needs encoding='utf-8' for non-english environment, error in playwright_controller.py
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp950' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 at position 11569 in page_script.js, triggered when MagenticOne WebSurfer initializes on a Chinese (cp950) Windows system. User provided exact reproduction command using Chinese input text, and identified the fix is adding encoding='utf-8' to the open() call.

signals.topic: AutoGen does not support custom OpenAI-compatible API endpoints via requests, only direct library calls
signals.summary: AutoGen's OpenAI client implementation only supports direct library calls and does not allow users to configure a custom endpoint URL. Users who need to route API requests through intermediate proxies or use custom OpenAI-compatible backends cannot do so with AutoGen.
signals.review_reason: User reports a blocking feature gap: AutoGen's OpenAI client does not accept a custom endpoint URL, preventing users from routing API calls through proxies or custom backends. This is a concrete, reproducible limitation that prevents legitimate multi-agent deployment architectures requiring custom endpoint routing.

source_issues.title: cant consume openai via requests
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states they need to consume an OpenAI instance via requests through an intermediate endpoint, but the AutoGen OpenAI implementation only supports direct library calls and does not expose a way to configure a custom endpoint URL. This is a feature gap that blocks a legitimate use case (API routing through proxy/custom backend).

signals.topic: Non-deterministic termination behavior in multi-agent loops reduces reproducibility and safety validation
signals.summary: Termination behavior in multi-agent loops varies with timing and tool-response ordering, causing non-deterministic termination reasons and step counts across repeated runs. This undermines reproducibility and makes safety guarantees harder to validate for autonomous agent loops.
signals.review_reason: Non-deterministic loop termination is a real reproducibility issue in autonomous multi-agent systems. For production deployments relying on AutoGen for autonomous workflows, unpredictable termination behavior represents a meaningful operational risk — users cannot reliably predict when agents stop, which directly impacts safety guarantees and operational control.

source_issues.title: Add deterministic termination contract tests for multi-agent loops
source_issues.evidence: User identified that equivalent multi-agent loop fixtures terminate with varying reasons and step counts across repeated runs. Provided minimal reproduction steps and a specific commit under test (13e144e5476a76ca0d76bf4f07a6401d133a03ed) on macOS Darwin 25.3.0 arm64 with Python 3.14.0. Identified the root cause as flaky timing assumptions in termination logic.

signals.topic: Dashboard screencast freezes permanently on frame acknowledgment failures with no error or recovery
signals.summary: When frame acknowledgment fails (network timeout, connection issues), the screencast protocol deadlocks because sendMayFail() silently swallows errors. Video freezes permanently, requiring full restart.
aliases: Screencast freezes on frame ack failure
Dashboard interactive clicks fail remote browsers screencast freeze
signals.review_reason: Dashboard is a core Playwright debugging/observability tool. A permanent freeze with no error message blocks the entire debugging workflow. Two separate issues confirm this as a real, recurring problem. Count=2 confirms it's not an isolated incident.

source_issues.title: # [Bug]: Dashboard screencast freezes on frame acknowledgment failures
source_issues.evidence: Root cause documented: sendMayFail() silently swallows all errors in the frame-ack protocol. Video freezes permanently with no error message and no recovery mechanism. Affects network timeouts, high latency, and connection interruptions.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Dashboard interactive clicks fail with remote browsers and screencast freezes
source_issues.evidence: Interactive clicks on remote browsers (connectOverCDP, Android, iOS) go to (0,0) instead of intended coordinates. Also independently confirms the screencast freeze bug from Bug 2.

signals.topic: MCP extension routes headed browser through launchApp, opening chromeless app-mode window instead of normal headed browser and dying between tool calls
signals.summary: Since v0.0.73, the MCP browser session routes through launchApp which unconditionally adds --app=data:text/html flag, making headed mode open a chromeless window without toolbar/tabs. Browser is also torn down between tool calls, breaking multi-step MCP workflows.
aliases: MCP headed mode uses app mode window
MCP headed browser dies between tool calls
MCP extension executable path ignored headed mode
signals.review_reason: MCP headed mode is fundamentally broken: window lacks normal browser controls, second tool call dies, and explicit executable path is ignored. These are multi-symptom failures of a single architectural regression since v0.0.73, directly blocking all headed-mode MCP use cases.

source_issues.title: [Bug] @playwright/mcp 0.0.73 routes headed browser through launchApp — chromeless --app= window, dies between tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis: launchApp unconditionally pushes --app=data:text/html on Chromium argv. MCP CLI exposes no flag to opt out. Regression from 0.0.72. Second tool call dies with 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. Includes reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Playwright MCP extension mode ignores explicit executable path
source_issues.evidence: Extension mode opens the wrong browser (host platform default) instead of the user-specified --executable-path. In WSL/CDE setups where the extension is installed in a Windows Edge profile, MCP requests time out with error -32001. Root cause: executablePath not passed from CLI through to CDPRelayServer.

signals.topic: routeFromHAR replay returns wrong/failed response due to duplicate HAR entries from retries
signals.summary: When HAR recording captures a retried request, both the failed and successful attempts are stored as duplicate entries for the same URL. On replay, Playwright matches the first (failed) entry, serving empty/corrupt content and causing test failures.
aliases: HAR replay empty body served instead of correct response
signals.review_reason: Primary test automation workflow is broken: HAR replay is a core Playwright feature used for offline/fast test execution. Duplicate entries on retries cause wrong content to be served silently, making tests pass/fail unpredictably. This directly blocks teams relying on HAR-based test fixtures.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: routeFromHAR records duplicate entries for retried requests, causing replay to serve failed response
source_issues.evidence: Retried requests produce duplicate HAR entries; replay always uses the first (failed) entry, causing blank pages and test failures. Includes minimal reproduction repo with record/replay steps.

signals.topic: HAR recording truncates cookie values containing '=' for API requests, corrupting recorded fixtures
signals.summary: The HAR recorder uses split('=') instead of indexOf('=') when parsing cookie headers for APIRequestContext, truncating Base64/JWT cookie values at the first '=' character.
aliases: HAR cookie value truncated base64 JWT
API request HAR recording broken cookie parsing
signals.review_reason: HAR recording — a primary feature for test fixture creation and offline replay — silently produces corrupted HAR files for any API request with cookie values containing '='. Users unknowingly record wrong fixture data, causing tests to fail on replay. Not P0 only because the HTTP request itself is unaffected.

source_issues.title: fix(har): API request cookie values containing '=' are truncated in HAR recording
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible code sample shows cookie 'token=abc=xyz' recorded as 'token=abc' in HAR. Root cause identified in fetch.ts using split('=') instead of indexOf. Affects Base64 tokens, JWTs, and URL-encoded values.

signals.topic: Zip Slip path traversal vulnerability in harUnzip allows arbitrary file write from malicious .har.zip
signals.summary: harUnzip writes zip entries using path.join(resourcesDir, entry) without validating the resolved path stays within resourcesDir, enabling path traversal attacks.
aliases: harUnzip path traversal arbitrary file write
signals.review_reason: Arbitrary file write is a high-severity security vulnerability. While the attack requires a user to load an untrusted .har.zip file, the risk is real in CI environments where shared artifacts are common. The fix pattern already exists in the codebase, making this actionable.

source_issues.title: Security: Zip Slip path traversal in harUnzip allows arbitrary file write
source_issues.evidence: Explicit vulnerability report with root cause in localUtils.ts line 190, comparing to safe implementation in extractTrace() that uses resolveWithinRoot(). Attack vector: malicious .har.zip file written to arbitrary filesystem locations.

signals.topic: SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync fails with NOT NULL constraint violation on json column
signals.summary: When calling UpsertAsync on a SqliteVectorStore collection, the operation throws 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json' because the connector serializes non-vector properties into a null or empty value, violating the NOT NULL constraint on the json column. Workarounds like manually providing non-empty string values still fail, and the only reliable bypass is raw SQL.
aliases: SqliteVec connector upsert fails json column null constraint
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete workflow runtime bug with a full reproducible code sample. The SqliteVectorStore UpsertAsync operation fails on every call with a NOT NULL constraint violation on the json column. Users cannot use the core SqliteVectorStore upsert functionality at all. Workarounds (explicit non-empty values, relaxed schema) fail. Only raw SQL bypasses the bug. This directly blocks users from storing vector data in SQLite via the Semantic Kernel connector.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: [SqliteVectorStore] NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json during UpsertAsync
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with provided C# sample: calling UpsertAsync on SqliteVectorStore with a valid record throws 'SQLite Error 19: NOT NULL constraint failed: words.json'. Tried workarounds (explicit non-empty values, relaxed schema) still fail. Manual raw SQL insert works. Affects both in-memory and file-based SQLite, and SqliteVec connector chunk tables.

signals.topic: Custom PromptExecutionSettings extended properties not serialized in HTTP request to vLLM OpenAI API server
signals.summary: When using a custom PromptExecutionSettings subclass with an extended property (e.g. 'guided_regex' for vLLM), the custom property is not included in the serialized HTTP request body sent to the vLLM server. The request reaches the server without the guided_decoding parameter, breaking structured output/guided decoding functionality.
aliases: vLLM guided_regex not sent in request
custom PromptExecutionSettings JSON property not serialized for vLLM
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug in the .NET vLLM connector where extended PromptExecutionSettings properties are silently dropped from the HTTP request. The user provides a full reproduction with server-side logs proving the guided_regex parameter never arrives. This breaks structured output workflows relying on guided decoding with vLLM. The bug is deterministic and reproducible. While only 1 issue, the impact is significant for users needing structured output with local vLLM models.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Custom PromptExecutionSettings with 'guided_regex' property for vLLM OpenAI Api Server is not working
source_issues.evidence: User provides full C# reproduction: a custom VllmCustomExecutionSettings extending OpenAIPromptExecutionSettings with a [JsonPropertyName('guided_regex')] property. The docker container log shows guided_decoding=None in received params instead of the expected GuidedDecodingParams with regex. The same feature works via Python openai package, proving the server supports it. The C# connector simply fails to serialize the extended property into the HTTP request body.

signals.topic: VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions not passed to EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions, blocking automatic embedding generation with MRL models
signals.summary: Users with text embedding models that support Model-Referenced Learning (MRL) cannot use Semantic Kernel's automatic embedding generation because VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions has no way to be propagated to EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions in the automatic embedding generation flow.
aliases: automatic embedding generation MRL dimensions not configurable
VectorStoreVectorAttribute Dimensions not propagated to embedding generation options
signals.review_reason: This issue blocks automatic embedding generation for MRL-capable embedding models. Users who need to control embedding dimensions (a common requirement for vector store compatibility and cost optimization) cannot do so through the automatic embedding generation flow. This forces manual embedding generation as a workaround, adding significant friction. While count=1, the blocking nature and the fact it is an open issue labeled 'stale' suggest a real gap in the API.

source_issues.title: `VectorStoreVectorAttribute.Dimensions` should be passed to `EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions`
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'while using text embedding models with MRL support, we could not use automatic embedding generation. It is because we have no way to specify EmbeddingGenerationOptions.Dimensions via automatic embedding generation flow.'

signals.topic: Browser Use fails in heartbeat automation turns due to IAB pipe ownership validation
signals.summary: Browser Use works in foreground user turns but fails in automated heartbeat turns with 'Browser turn does not belong to this IAB pipe' error, blocking scheduled automation workflows that depend on in-app browser.
aliases: IAB pipe validation error in heartbeat turns
signals.review_reason: User-facing workflow failure that blocks automated Browser Use scenarios. The automation feature is a core use case, and its complete failure to run constitutes a significant service degradation.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop heartbeat automations fail Browser Use with 'Browser turn does not belong to this IAB pipe'
source_issues.evidence: Heartbeat automation fails immediately with IAB pipe ownership error when attempting to run the same Browser Use flow that succeeds in foreground user turns.

signals.topic: Pro subscription upgrade not recognized; users remain locked out with 'out of messages' error
signals.summary: Users who upgrade to Pro still see 'You're out of Codex messages' despite payment, with no resolution after logout/login/restart and waiting up to half a day.
signals.review_reason: Direct cost loss: user paid for Pro but cannot use the service. Main flow is completely blocked with no workaround. Despite count=1, the evidence of paid-feature unavailability is unambiguous — this is a billing-service sync failure that leaves paying customers locked out.

source_issues.title: I upgraded to Pro but I still see "You're out of Codex messages"
source_issues.evidence: User paid for Pro upgrade but cannot access the service. Tried standard troubleshooting steps including logout, login, restart, and waiting half a day without resolution.

signals.topic: GPT-5.5 produces gibberish garbage output in Codex CLI
signals.summary: Codex CLI with GPT-5.5 model produces incomprehensible gibberish output instead of coherent responses, making the service completely unusable for affected users.
signals.review_reason: Significant experience degradation where the model produces completely unusable output. The primary workflow is fundamentally broken for affected users using GPT-5.5.

source_issues.title: Garbage output
source_issues.evidence: User reports gibberish output from GPT-5.5 on macOS CLI, with a reproducible uploaded thread session. Model output is completely incoherent and unusable.

signals.topic: Codex CLI abandons interrupted task instead of resuming after separate request
signals.summary: When Codex is interrupted mid-task by a separate request, it handles the interruption then stops completely rather than returning to the prior work, losing the active task context.
signals.review_reason: Session state issue where user work is abandoned after interruption. Clear workflow disruption — the user's prior task context is lost, wasting prior effort.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI may be nerd-sniped handling an interruption instead of resuming prior work
source_issues.evidence: When user interrupts Codex mid-task with a separate request, Codex stops rather than preserving and returning to the active task stack, abandoning the original work.

signals.topic: Dictation audio permanently lost when transcription exceeds length limit
signals.summary: Codex Desktop accepts long voice recordings (20–30 minutes) but cannot transcribe them, fails with Retry state, then permanently loses the original audio with no user recovery path.
signals.review_reason: Permanent data loss with no recovery path. User's spoken work is accepted then completely lost with no user-facing recovery mechanism. This is a critical failure that directly causes irrecoverable user data loss.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop dictation accepts long recordings it cannot transcribe, then loses unrecoverable audio
source_issues.evidence: User lost 20–30 minutes of important business dictation when ASR failed and audio was not recoverable. High-impact data loss with no recovery path.

signals.topic: Session data loss — conversation history silently lost in multiple scenarios
signals.summary: OpenAIConversationsSession and OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession silently lose session items: assistant items vanish without error, history disappears after failed compaction, and retry cleanup deletes unrelated items. Users lose full conversation context without any signal.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct session code paths all result in silent data loss of conversation context. Impact is severe: users lose all prior conversation history with no error signal, forcing them to re-explain context and causing workflow restarts. Affects core session functionality.

source_issues.title: OpenAIConversationsSession loses prior assistant items
source_issues.evidence: Session silently drops prior assistant items with no error returned. Related to previously fixed item-shape mismatches (#1709, #1882).

source_issues.title: OpenAIResponsesCompactionSession can lose session history if add_items fails after clear
source_issues.evidence: Compaction clears underlying session then fails on writing compacted items, leaving session empty with no history retained.

source_issues.title: rewind_session_items can delete unrelated tail session items during retry cleanup
source_issues.evidence: Rewind logic calls pop_item() before confirm, deleting items from wrong retry context and leaving session in corrupted state.

signals.topic: Chat Completions streaming output_index bugs — duplicate output_index values
signals.summary: Chat Completions streaming handler produces incorrect output_index values: a boolean is passed where an integer is expected, and fallback tool call paths reuse output_index values causing duplicates. These bugs corrupt streaming message structure.
aliases: duplicate output_index in fallback tool calls
signals.review_reason: Two distinct bugs in the Chat Completions streaming handler cause structural data corruption (wrong type for output_index, duplicate values). While not a complete flow block, these cause malformed streaming events that downstream consumers cannot parse correctly. Count=2 supports inclusion at P2.

source_issues.title: Chat Completions streaming computes assistant output_index with a bool expression
source_issues.evidence: state.reasoning_content_index_ (boolean) is passed as output_index (requires integer). Event constructors receive wrong type, corrupting streaming output structure.

source_issues.title: Chat Completions streaming fallback tool calls can reuse output_index
source_issues.evidence: Fallback branch for non-streamed function calls recomputes output_index, producing duplicate values across multiple function calls. Breaks downstream message parsing.

signals.topic: WebSocket connection rejected with HTTP 401 — all requests fail
signals.summary: Users' WebSocket connections to the OpenAI Agents SDK are rejected with HTTP 401, making the entire websocket transport unusable and blocking all agent requests. Previously working HTTP long-polling also stopped, leaving users with no functional transport path.
signals.review_reason: Main flow completely blocked: both WebSocket and HTTP transports fail, making the agent SDK unusable for production. Explicit user evidence of service-wide disruption with multiple affected requests per day.

source_issues.title: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 401
source_issues.evidence: All websocket requests fail with HTTP 401. HTTP long-polling also stopped working. User reports main production path is blocked with no alternative. Labeled as server issue, 2 comments confirming ongoing impact.

signals.topic: Tool executes after is_enabled becomes false — authorization control bypassed
signals.summary: A function tool with is_enabled=False is still executed if it was visible to the model before being disabled. The is_enabled guard is checked at visibility time but not at execution time, allowing tools to run against the user's explicit revocation.
aliases: tool disable does not stop execution
signals.review_reason: Explicit authorization control (is_enabled) is bypassed, allowing tool execution after user revocation. This is a clear authorization gap affecting any workflow that dynamically controls tool availability. The tool can trigger real-world actions the user has explicitly disabled.

source_issues.title: Dynamic function tool is still executed after is_enabled becomes false
source_issues.evidence: Tool executes despite is_enabled returning False. Authorization control is silently bypassed — real-world actions can be triggered after user has revoked access.

signals.topic: coerce_shell_call splits string command into character list — silent wrong behavior
signals.summary: Passing a string command to the shell tool results in the string being split into a character list instead of being treated as a single command or rejected. The result is a silently wrong shell call with incorrect arguments, causing unexpected shell behavior.
signals.review_reason: Shell tool silently executes wrong command structure. Instead of treating a string as one command or rejecting it, it splits into individual characters passed as separate arguments. Users get unexpected shell behavior with no error, making this a silent failure that is hard to debug.

source_issues.title: coerce_shell_call splits string commands into character lists
source_issues.evidence: coerce_shell_call() treats string-valued action.commands as a generic Sequence, normalizing 'echo hi' into ['e','c','h','o',' ','h','i'] instead of rejecting it. No error raised, wrong shell behavior.

signals.topic: Responses stream accumulator crashes with AttributeError when response.output_item.added has item=None
signals.summary: The Responses streaming accumulator in _responses.py dereferences event.item.type without guarding against item=None, causing AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type'. This crashes the SDK for users of OpenAI-compatible custom providers that emit malformed/partial Responses stream events.
signals.review_reason: Hard crash (AttributeError) that blocks the main Responses streaming flow for users of OpenAI-compatible custom providers. The SDK crashes unconditionally before app-level error handling can run.

source_issues.title: Responses stream accumulator crashes when response.output_item.added has item=None
source_issues.evidence: Crashes with AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type' inside the SDK stream accumulator before application-level code can recover. Triggered by any OpenAI-compatible custom provider emitting item=None in response.output_item.added.

signals.topic: Realtime tool calls with MCP server not executing — tool calls silently skipped
signals.summary: When using Realtime API with MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, tool calls are never executed. The session appears functional but all tool invocations are silently skipped with no error, blocking the entire Realtime+MCP use case.
aliases: Realtime MCP tool calls not working
WebSocket realtime MCP server tools skipped
signals.review_reason: Key Realtime API feature (MCP tool execution) is entirely non-functional. This is a main-flow blocking issue for Realtime+MCP users, though root cause is still being investigated and may involve server-side behavior.

source_issues.title: Realtime does not execute tool calls with mcp
source_issues.evidence: User reports MCP tools work with npx inspector but are never executed via the Python SDK Realtime API. Only the initial instruction greeting appears; tool calls are silently skipped with no error or log.

signals.topic: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk accumulate incorrectly — produces invalid JSON
signals.summary: When speculative decoding or certain providers send multiple tool_calls entries with the same index in the first streamed chunk, the accumulate_delta logic merges by physical list position rather than logical index, resulting in duplicated entries and broken/malformed tool call arguments in the final output.
aliases: Streaming tool_call index merge by position not logical index
signals.review_reason: Main streaming flow produces silently corrupted tool call output when the API sends duplicate-index entries. Arguments are partially lost and final JSON is invalid, breaking tool use end-to-end. Reproducible with vLLM OpenAI-compatible server using speculative decoding.

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: accumulate_delta assumes index field matches physical list position. First chunk with two index:0 entries stores both physically, subsequent chunks merge into acc_value[0] while the duplicate remains separate, stranding partial tool call arguments and producing invalid final JSON.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely with file stuck at in_progress
signals.summary: upload_and_poll() blocks forever because the vector store file gets stuck in status='in_progress' indefinitely, while the underlying raw file already shows status='processed'. No error is returned, no timeout occurs, and last_error stays null, making it impossible to detect or recover from this state.
aliases: vector store file processing hangs forever
signals.review_reason: Key SDK polling method (upload_and_poll) blocks indefinitely with no error signal and no recovery path. Users have no way to detect or work around the stuck state, making this a main-flow blocker for vector store file processing.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely. Observed: raw file is 'processed' but vector_store_file stays 'in_progress' forever with last_error=null. No timeout, no error, no way to detect the stuck state programmatically.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers when deserializing responses
signals.summary: With pydantic 2.12+ and DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD, ~0.6% of requests fail in forkserver workers due to PydanticUserError during deserialization. With eager build (DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false), ~9.5% of forkserver workers permanently fail at import time, causing all their requests to fail. Root cause is hardcoded _parent_namespace_depth=5 in model_rebuild causing silent failures in certain call stack contexts.
signals.review_reason: Production-impacting crash causing 0.6-9.5% request failures in high-volume multiprocess environments. The PydanticUserError is thrown inside SDK deserialization before app code can catch it. At scale, even 0.6% failure rate represents thousands of failed requests per million.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: 0.6% error rate with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true, 9.5% error rate with false. Errors grow over time. In production with millions of requests, this causes significant request failures. Traceback shows exact call chain: construct() → _get_extra_fields_type() → schema['type'] == 'model' → _get_built() → raises PydanticUserError.

signals.topic: Generic runtime controls (timeout, thinking) fail in OpenClaw/acpx-managed Claude ACP sessions due to config option key mismatches
signals.summary: OpenClaw sends ACP config keys (timeout, thinking, approval_policy) that Claude ACP does not advertise, causing runtime control features to fail with Internal error/ACP_TURN_FAILED. Clean/model-only prompts work, but core workflow features (reasoning effort control, session timeout) are blocked.
aliases: ACP config option key mismatch blocks runtime controls
session/set_config_option forwarding failures with Claude ACP
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user pain point. The issue documents a reproducible failure pattern where OpenClaw's ACP runtime controls (timeout, thinking/effort, approval_policy) all fail with Internal error because config option key names do not match what the Claude ACP adapter advertises. The user impact is concrete: core workflow features—reasoning effort control and session timeout—are completely unusable through the acpx backend. While only 1 issue is in scope, the evidence includes a detailed multi-case smoke test matrix showing systematic failure vs. passing cases, and the bug reproduces across current-version stack. The count is 1 because the dataset only covers openclaw/acpx; the issue itself cross-references openclaw/openclaw#73875. Confidence is 0.75 (not higher) because single-source, single-user report without other corroborating accounts.

source_issues.title: Claude ACP config option handling: generic runtime controls fail while clean/model-only path works
source_issues.evidence: Smoke test matrix shows timeoutSeconds, thinking:medium, thinking:high, and combined model+thinking all fail with AcpRuntimeError: Internal error / ACP_TURN_FAILED. Clean prompt and model-only overrides succeed. The failure is reproducible across multiple test cases in a single session. Root cause: OpenClaw maps timeoutSeconds->timeout (not advertised), thinking->thinking (Claude ACP advertises 'effort' instead), and approval_policy (not advertised). This blocks the primary use case of applying runtime controls to Claude ACP sessions via acpx.

signals.topic: ClawScan false positives on legitimate skills cause published skills to be incorrectly flagged as suspicious, forcing maintainers through lengthy appeals
signals.summary: Multiple legitimate skills (FreeRide, modelscope-api, markdown2doc, architecture-critic, opencode-zen-check-free-models) are incorrectly flagged by ClawScan's static analysis, marked as Suspicious or subject to review warnings. Self-scan results contradict ClawScan findings. Maintainers must file appeals to restore their skills.
signals.review_reason: Repeatedly occurring false positive pattern affecting multiple skill publishers. Legitimate skills are suppressed from public listings, causing direct harm to publishers (lost visibility, downloads, reputation). The FreeRide case shows the scanner re-flagging the same skill on every release with identical findings — indicating a systemic quality defect, not edge-case noise.

source_issues.title: [False Positive] - ClawScan re-flags FreeRide on every release with findings that conflate documented purpose with actual risk
source_issues.evidence: FreeRide re-flagged on every release with identical five findings despite zero behavior change. Self-scan shows no issues. Maintainer calls it 'unsustainable' and says it 'generates pure noise'.

source_issues.title: [False Positive] - Skill Flagged as sensitive, just for checking URL and alerting user
source_issues.evidence: Skill flagged as sensitive for simply checking a URL and alerting user.

source_issues.title: False Positive: My Skill 'modelscope-api' was incorrectly flagged as Suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Skill marked as Suspicious (suppressed in public listing). Official self-scan 'npx clawvet scan' shows NO security issues. Maintainer requests removal of false flag.

source_issues.title: [Skill Appeal] markdown2doc incorrectly flagged as suspicious
source_issues.evidence: Skill incorrectly flagged as suspicious by ClawScan. VirusTotal and OpenClaw scans show normal results. Maintainer requests label removal.

source_issues.title: False positive: architecture-critic — API key reading code flagged incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: Static analysis flags legitimate config-reading code as API key exfiltration. Code reads user's existing OpenClaw config to find provider key; does not exfiltrate or store credentials.

signals.topic: home-assistant-control skill: ha_call.sh bypasses all safety confirmation checks declared in ha_safe_action.sh, enabling unauthorized actuator control
signals.summary: The skill ships two paths to the same Home Assistant API: ha_safe_action.sh has domain checks and confirmation prompts, but ha_call.sh accepts arbitrary method/path/data with zero checks. An agent can directly call /api/services/lock/unlock or /alarm_disarm bypassing all declared safety controls.
signals.review_reason: Direct user safety impact: an agent using this skill can bypass all confirmation checks and perform high-impact physical actions (unlock doors, disarm alarms) without user knowledge. The skill explicitly promises 'Confirm before high-impact actions' but the existence of ha_call.sh makes that promise hollow. This is not theoretical — the bypass path is shipped in the published skill.

source_issues.title: security: skill home-assistant-control: Unguarded API Caller Bypasses All Safety Checks
source_issues.evidence: ha_call.sh accepts arbitrary HTTP method, path and JSON data with no entity-level safety checks or confirmation prompts. A user can instruct their agent to directly unlock a door without any confirmation, contradicting the skill's declared safety property.

signals.topic: binance-dca-tool skill: No user confirmation guardrail before executing real financial trades — agent can place buy orders without asking
signals.summary: The skill executes real market buy orders on Binance. Its only guardrails address credential storage; there is no guardrail requiring user confirmation before placing a trade. The agent proceeds after basic environment checks, potentially causing financial loss.
signals.review_reason: Direct financial harm risk: the skill places real market buy orders with no confirmation step. A user relying on this skill could have their agent execute unauthorized trades, resulting in real monetary loss. The issue explicitly shows the agent proceeds without confirmation, and the spec has no guardrail preventing it.

source_issues.title: security: skill binance-dca-tool skip Has No Confirmation Guardrail
source_issues.evidence: The agent runs 'dca.sh buy BTCUSDT 50' with no confirmation prompt. The spec's only guardrails are about credential handling — neither mentions trade confirmation. The agent proceeds after basic environment checks, creating direct financial risk for users.

signals.topic: Inconsistent skill search results between homepage and /skills page due to different nonSuspiciousOnly filter defaults
signals.summary: Searching the same keyword on the homepage returns fewer results than on /skills. Root cause: unified search hardcodes nonSuspiciousOnly:true while /skills defaults to false, so suspicious skills are filtered differently. Users may believe a skill is missing when it is merely filtered.
aliases: unified search vs skills page discrepancy
signals.review_reason: Confirmed UX bug with clear user impact: the same query produces materially different results across two entry points, with no UI explanation. Users cannot trust homepage search to be complete, and publishers cannot understand why their skills appear in /skills but not in search. The issue includes exact file-level root cause citations.

source_issues.title: Inconsistent skill search results between homepage search and /skills
source_issues.evidence: Query '国泰海通' returns 1 result on homepage but 6 results on /skills. Both search the same backend; the inconsistency is caused by different nonSuspiciousOnly defaults in two frontend search implementations.

signals.topic: GitHub OAuth login loop blocks publishers from submitting skills — automated publishing flow is broken
signals.summary: A publisher (janeXlab) cannot publish skill jjr-iot-skill v1.3.1 because they hit a GitHub OAuth login loop on both the CLI and the website. The automated publishing flow is entirely blocked, forcing manual intervention.
signals.review_reason: Main publishing workflow is completely blocked for the affected user. The skill cannot be published through any automated path — this is a hard workflow failure, not a degraded experience. For a marketplace platform, inability to submit skills is a critical platform-availability issue.

source_issues.title: [Submission] jjr-iot-skill v1.3.1 - Agriculture IoT Integration
source_issues.evidence: Publisher hitting 'GitHub OAuth login loop on the CLI and website.' Automated publishing flow is blocked. Publisher must request manual indexing as workaround.

signals.topic: WSL local gateway onboarding is blocked by multiple validation and credential issues
signals.summary: WSL local gateway onboarding flow fails at operator pairing due to validation script isolation bugs, stale executable paths, and token resolution conflicts, preventing users from completing first-run setup.
aliases: operator pairing fails after gateway start
signals.review_reason: WSL local gateway onboarding is a primary first-run flow. The issue documents 8 specific blocking sub-problems: validation isolation writes to real user settings (contaminating credentials), launches stale executable, fails operator pairing, has token redaction gaps, uses a weak wsl.conf probe, has docs/implementation mismatch, leaks WSL processes on cancellation, and has legacy token confusion. This is a clear main-flow block with explicit evidence of flow failure during actual user onboarding.

source_issues.title: WSL local gateway onboarding validation blockers from PR #274
source_issues.evidence: Validation harness writes to real %APPDATA%\OpenClawTray\settings.json instead of isolated run folder, causing credential contamination and operator_auth_failed. 8 distinct blocking sub-items confirmed: validation isolation env var mismatch, stale exe path, pairing auth failure, token redaction gaps, weak wsl.conf probe, docs mismatch, cancellation leaks, legacy token confusion. Main onboarding flow is completely blocked.

signals.topic: Quick Send dialog titlebar mismatch and focus/z-order blocking tray menu interactions
signals.summary: Quick Send dialog does not use custom titlebar (unlike Hub/Canvas), ignores dark mode styling, stays on top of z-order, and blocks tray menu flyout from opening, requiring manual Escape/Cancel to dismiss.
aliases: tray menu flyout blocked by Quick Send
signals.review_reason: Quick Send dialog blocks the tray right-click menu flyout from appearing — this is a UI interaction regression that forces users to manually dismiss the dialog before they can access the tray menu. The dark mode titlebar mismatch also creates visual inconsistency. While not a full app crash, it is a recurring UX blocking behavior during normal tray interaction.

source_issues.title: Quick Send dialog: titlebar styling mismatch, focus/z-order issues
source_issues.evidence: Quick Send does not extend content into titlebar like Hub/Canvas windows, resulting in mismatched system titlebar with no dark mode support. The dialog stays on top of z-order and does not light-dismiss; when user opens tray right-click flyout while Quick Send is open, the flyout immediately dismisses because focus returns to Quick Send. Only way to dismiss is manual Escape or Cancel.

signals.topic: Tray menu flyout renders squished after Windows display DPI/scaling change
signals.summary: When Windows display scaling is changed while the tray app is running, the right-click context menu renders squished/compressed on first open after the DPI change, requiring a dismiss-and-reopen cycle to fix.
aliases: DPI change causes squished tray menu
tray menu compressed after scaling change
signals.review_reason: The tray menu rendering squished after DPI change is a visual regression that requires a dismiss-and-reopen workaround. It is reproducible across multiple scaling levels but is a transient UX issue (second open renders correctly), making it P2 rather than P1.

source_issues.title: Tray menu flyout renders squished after display scaling change until dismissed and reopened
source_issues.evidence: TrayMenuWindow reuses same instance across DPI changes. SizeToContent() calls MenuPanel.Measure() which returns stale layout values from previous DPI before XAML layout pass re-renders at new scale. Menu renders squished/compressed on first open post-DPI-change. Reproduced at 100%, 125%, 150%, 200% scaling on Windows 11 ARM64.

signals.topic: Onboarding white/light cards render unreadable white-on-white text in dark mode
signals.summary: Multiple onboarding surfaces use hard-coded white backgrounds (#FFFFFF) without explicit foreground text color, causing text to render white-on-white in dark mode, making onboarding pages unreadable.
aliases: white card foreground not set in dark theme
signals.review_reason: White-on-white text in dark mode is a critical accessibility failure during the onboarding flow — users cannot read card text content. The same root cause was previously fixed for yellow cards (#257), confirming the pattern is real and the fix approach is known. Since it affects a planned sequential flow (onboarding pages), it blocks the setup experience for dark mode users.

source_issues.title: Onboarding: white/light cards render unreadable text in dark mode (PR 241 follow-up)
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as previously fixed yellow card dark-mode bug — hard-coded light backgrounds (#FFFFFF for white cards, #E8F4FD for blue cards) with no explicit foreground, so system theme foreground (white) bleeds through and renders white-on-white in dark mode. Affects OnboardingCard base widget, WizardStepView text/select/multiselect cards, PermissionsPage, ConnectionPage, ReadyPage feature rows, WizardPage content card, and all blue info cards.

signals.topic: Chat textbox does not auto-focus when window opens, requiring manual click
signals.summary: Chat textbox does not receive focus when the chat window is opened via tray icon left-click or context menu, forcing users to manually click the textbox before typing.
signals.review_reason: Chat is a core interaction surface. The absence of auto-focus creates a friction step on every chat open — user tries to type immediately and nothing happens. This is a recurring UX degradation, though not a flow block.

source_issues.title: Chat textbox should auto-focus when window opens
source_issues.evidence: ShowNearTray() in ChatWindow.xaml.cs calls SetForegroundWindow to bring the window to foreground but does not call Focus() on the chat input element. User must manually click into the textbox before typing. Clear UX friction on a core interaction path.

signals.topic: /status displays incorrect information for claude-cli runtime sessions
signals.summary: Context display shows '?/800k' despite valid per-turn usage data in session. Auth label shows 'unknown' for working claude-cli sessions. totalTokensFresh stays false because Claude CLI reports usage components but no top-level totalTokens field.
signals.review_reason: Experience degradation: /status shows incorrect/unknown values for working sessions. Users cannot trust status display for monitoring. Multiple display issues across different status fields for the same runtime.

source_issues.title: claude-cli runtime sessions show "?/<limit>" for context usage in /status
source_issues.evidence: Context display shows '?/800k' despite valid per-turn usage data in session. totalTokensFresh stays false because Claude CLI reports usage components but no top-level totalTokens field.

source_issues.evidence: Auth label shows 'unknown' for working claude-cli sessions. No analogous credential probe for claude-cli provider in model-auth-label.ts despite reader existing and being used elsewhere.

signals.topic: Windows EPERM causes memory index --force to fail completely
signals.summary: Memory reindex consistently fails with EPERM on Windows 11 in v2026.5.5 and v2026.5.6. Reproducible with gateway running AND stopped. No workaround except manual dist patching.
aliases: Windows file rename failure memory index
signals.review_reason: Main workflow failure: memory index --force is completely blocked on Windows. Affects core memory management functionality. Users must manually patch compiled dist files as workaround. Reproducible on two consecutive versions.

source_issues.title: fix(memory): EPERM on Windows persists after 64187 retry — needs copyFile/unlink fallback (was in closed PR 71611)
source_issues.evidence: Memory reindex consistently fails with EPERM on Windows 11 in v2026.5.5 and v2026.5.6. Reproducible with gateway running AND stopped. No workaround except manual dist patching.

source_issues.title: Discord can go silent after 2026.5.5 upgrade/doctor model-runtime migration despite connected bot and working send path
source_issues.evidence: Discord connected, inbound messages accepted, manual send works, but normal agent replies silently fail. User-visible: bot present but no replies. Repair required inspecting model-runtime migration state, stale tasks, session overrides, and send path separately.

signals.summary: NVIDIA API does not support thinking parameter. OpenClaw auto-sets thinking=medium and the bot hangs, returning 100% cached response. Bot unusable with NVIDIA custom provider as primary model. Severity: High — blocks all responses. Frequency: Always.
aliases: NVIDIA provider thinking parameter not supported hangs
custom provider thinking parameter blocks responses
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking: NVIDIA custom provider is a primary model option. When used, the bot is completely unusable (100% cached responses). No way to disable thinking per provider.

signals.topic: pip install fails on Python 3.13+ due to tiktoken/PyO3 version incompatibility
signals.summary: Installation via pip/uvx fails on Python 3.13, 3.13.2, and 3.14 because the tiktoken dependency's PyO3 version (0.20.3) only supports Python up to 3.12, blocking users from installing the tool entirely.
aliases: pip install blocked by tiktoken build failure
signals.review_reason: Three distinct users across Windows 11 (Python 3.14.3, Python 3.13.2) and macOS (Python 3.13) all report the same root cause: tiktoken's PyO3-ffi v0.20.3 blocks installation on Python 3.13+. This is a high-frequency (count=3) main-flow blocker — users cannot even install the tool, making it a critical P0 pain point with clear user impact evidence including explicit frustration ('useless for me', 'so sad').

source_issues.title: cant install on windows 11
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows 11 with Python 3.14.3 reports: 'in 2026 we still not have easy install, so sad... useless for me.' Failed to build tiktoken wheel due to PyO3 max Python version 3.12 vs actual 3.14.

source_issues.title: Error Installing via Pip on Python 3.13.2
source_issues.evidence: User on Windows 11 with Python 3.13.2 reports installation failure: 'error: the configured Python interpreter version (3.13) is newer than PyO3's maximum supported version (3.12)'. Failed to build tiktoken.

source_issues.title: Python 3.13 is unsupported
source_issues.evidence: User on macOS 15.1.1 with Python 3.13 reports: 'Failed to download and build tiktoken==0.7.0'. PyO3 maximum supported version is 3.12. Same issue on Windows. 4 comments from other users confirming the problem.

signals.topic: litellm dependency conflicts causing ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError crashes on Windows
signals.summary: litellm dependency chain (greenlet DLL, openai._models) fails on Windows, causing aider to crash with ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError at startup or during use.
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues all rooted in litellm dependency failures on Windows. Each causes aider to crash — either at startup or during message processing — making the tool completely unusable for affected Windows users. Multiple distinct failure points in the litellm import chain confirm a systemic Windows compatibility problem, not isolated incidents.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ImportError in __init__.py line 29
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: DLL load failed while importing _greenlet: The specified module could not be found. Windows 10, CPython, no virtual environment. Aider crashes at startup when invoking web scraping (playwright -> greenlet).

source_issues.title: Uncaught ModuleNotFoundError in base.py line 3
source_issues.evidence: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'openai._models' during LiteLLMExceptions initialization. Windows 11, CPython. Aider crashes at runtime when processing messages.

source_issues.title: Aetheria
source_issues.evidence: FileNotFoundError: litellm tokenizer JSON file missing on Windows Python install. Aider fails to start on Windows 11 due to missing litellm resource file.

signals.topic: Uncaught ValueError crash when litellm introduces new exception types
signals.summary: When litellm adds new exception classes not tracked in aider's exception list, aider raises an uncaught ValueError and crashes during message processing.
aliases: exception list out of sync with litellm
signals.review_reason: Single issue but represents a structural fragility: aider's exception list must be manually kept in sync with litellm's growing exception set. Every new litellm exception will break aider until someone manually updates exceptions.py. This is a recurring pattern — not a one-off.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ValueError in exceptions.py line 71
source_issues.evidence: ValueError: PermissionDeniedError is in litellm but not in aider's exceptions list. Crash occurs at LiteLLMExceptions init during send_message, blocking user interaction mid-session. Windows 11 user. Closed as fixed.

signals.topic: Uncaught tree-sitter QueryError crash during repo-map generation
signals.summary: Aider crashes with an uncaught QueryError when tree-sitter encounters an invalid node type during repo-map tag extraction, blocking the core repo-map feature.
signals.review_reason: Aider crashes at the start of a session during repo-map generation — the feature users rely on for codebase context. The QueryError is uncaught and propagates to the top level, fully blocking the main workflow.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module. Crash occurs during get_ranked_tags in repo-map generation. Linux user. Aider crashes before any meaningful work begins.

signals.topic: OSError crash when command-line arguments exceed OS filename length limit
signals.summary: Long --extra-system-prompt values cause OSError 'File name too long' when pathlib attempts to stat the argument as a file path, crashing aider at startup.
aliases: pathlib stat crash on long args
signals.review_reason: Users who use long system prompts (e.g., long instruction sets or rules) encounter a crash at startup. While count=1, the crash is direct and preventable — aider should not treat command-line arguments as file paths.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 842
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long. Triggered by passing a long --extra-system-prompt argument. Aider crashes immediately at startup in main.py before any useful work can begin.

signals.topic: Realtime models (openai:realtime:*) 不支持 tool/function calling，导致关键评估功能与 chat 模型不等效
signals.summary: 当使用 openai:realtime:* 提供商时，配置的 tool/function calling 完全不触发，而相同的 openai:chat:* 提供商可正常调用工具。这导致无法对 realtime 模型进行工具调用评估，核心功能在 realtime 场景下不可用。
signals.review_reason: 核心评估功能在 realtime 模型上不可用。用户报告必现 bug（相同配置仅切换 chat→realtime 即触发），且 tool calling 是 promptfoo 关键评估能力，其失效导致 realtime 模型无法进行工具调用验证，属于关键功能不可用场景。

source_issues.title: Realtime models do not trigger tool calls
source_issues.evidence: 同一测试用例（相同的 tools.yaml、prompts、assertions），chat 模型正常调用工具，realtime 模型返回纯文本而不调用工具。问题为必现（reproducible），且影响所有 realtime 模型（gpt-realtime 等）。

signals.topic: OpenAI embedding 提供商忽略 passthrough 参数，无法控制 dimensions 等关键配置
signals.summary: OpenAI embedding provider 完全忽略 passthrough 参数，对比同代码库中 responses API provider 正确处理 passthrough 的行为，存在明显不一致。这导致用户无法在 RAG 评估中配置 embedding dimensions，阻断特定 RAG 评估场景。
signals.review_reason: 明确的代码级 bug（embedding.ts 某行忽略了 passthrough），导致用户在 RAG 评估中无法配置 embedding dimensions，而用户明确表示该功能对比较 RAG pipeline 性能至关重要。同一代码库中 responses API provider 正确实现了 passthrough，存在实现不一致，为真实 bug 而非设计问题。

source_issues.title: Bug: OpenAI embeddings ignore passthrough
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供代码引用（embedding.ts L30-34 vs responses.ts L386），明确指出 embedding.ts 忽略 passthrough 而 responses.ts 正确处理。issue 已 closed（确认修复或接受）。用户意图对比 RAG pipeline 的不同 dimensions 以评估性能，passthrough 被忽略导致此评估场景完全无法工作。

signals.topic: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk 提供商在后台 sub-agent 发送 result 消息时提前返回错误结果
signals.summary: 当使用 anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider 并触发后台 sub-agent 时，provider 在第一个 result 消息（sub-agent 的结果）处立即返回，而非等待 main agent 的最终结果。这导致 promptfoo eval 输出的不是主 agent 的真实最终回复，而是子 agent 的摘要，完全破坏了评估的正确性。
aliases: claude-agent-sdk returns early on sub-agent result
background agent result message causes premature return
signals.review_reason: 评估结果正确性被破坏——provider 返回子 agent 摘要而非主 agent 最终回复，导致所有涉及后台 sub-agent 的评估结果均不正确。这是主流程阻断级别的 bug，用户提供了精确的代码位置和修复建议，问题机制清晰可复现。issue 已 closed 说明确认了问题的存在。

source_issues.title: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider returns early when background sub-agents emit result messages
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供精确代码位置（src/providers/claude-agent-sdk.ts L1024-L1080），明确指出 for-await 循环在遇到第一个 result 消息时执行 return 语句（L1073）导致提前退出。issue 已 closed（接受修复建议）。影响场景：使用 Task/Agent 工具触发后台 sub-agent 的任何 promptfoo 评估。

signals.topic: Bedrock Converse streaming returns `tool_kwargs` as JSON string instead of dict, breaking cross-provider tool-call workflows
signals.summary: The Bedrock Converse streaming adapter constructs ToolCallBlock objects with tool_kwargs as a raw JSON string instead of a parsed dict. This causes Pydantic ValidationError in downstream providers (e.g., Google GenAI adapter) that expect a dict, and breaks any workflow that persists chat history from a Bedrock streaming session and replays it through another provider.
signals.review_reason: Clear main-flow failure: Pydantic ValidationError at runtime when ToolCallBlock with string tool_kwargs is consumed by another adapter. Breaks multi-provider agent workflows that are a core use case. Has reproduction steps and exact code locations. Not P0 because count=1 and no other issues corroborate the same root cause.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Bedrock Converse streaming produces string `tool_kwargs` in `ToolCallBlock` instead of dict
source_issues.evidence: Cross-provider workflows break: Google GenAI adapter receives ToolCallBlock with string tool_kwargs and raises pydantic_core.ValidationError. Pattern appears in 6 locations in base.py streaming code paths. Any workflow persisting Bedrock streaming chat history and replaying through another provider hits this.

signals.topic: ContextVar not propagated in non-async FunctionTool execution, breaking OpenTelemetry distributed tracing
signals.summary: When using sync (non-async) FunctionTools, Python ContextVars set by the calling context are not readable within the tool. This causes OpenTelemetry tracing to show orphan spans because the ContextVar used for span parenting is not accessible in sync tool calls. Async tools work correctly.
aliases: OpenTelemetry orphan spans in sync tool calls
ContextVar propagation broken in FunctionTool fn path
signals.review_reason: Significant user impact for observability: OpenTelemetry tracing (a standard production tool) is broken for all sync FunctionTool use cases. Users cannot correctly parent spans, making distributed tracing unusable. Not P0 because count=1 and the issue is scoped to observability rather than main-flow data correctness.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `ContextVar` not propagated on non-`async` tool execution.
source_issues.evidence: OpenTelemetry users: all non-async tool calls produce orphan spans because the ContextVar used for span parenting is not propagated. Includes unit test that reproduces the issue. llama-index core >=0.14.18 affected.

signals.topic: Arbitrary file read via `ImageDocument.metadata['file_path']` bypassing constructor validation
signals.summary: image_documents_to_base64 in llama-index-core reads arbitrary files through ImageDocument.metadata['file_path'] without path allow-listing, symlink checks, or MIME validation. Since metadata is a free-form dict not gated by the constructor's is_image_pil check, attackers can read /etc/passwd, ~/.aws/credentials, .env files, and K8s service account tokens. The encoded bytes are forwarded to the multimodal LLM and echoed back when asked to describe the 'image'.
aliases: Unrestricted file path in ImageDocument metadata
signals.review_reason: Severe user impact: arbitrary file read primitive reachable in any application that passes user-influenced data into ImageDocument metadata. Demonstrably reads sensitive files (AWS credentials, K8s tokens) and echoes contents via LLM. Despite the project classifying path traversal from untrusted paths as application-layer responsibility, the author explicitly chose to file publicly with detailed evidence; the vulnerability is real and impacts production deployments.

source_issues.title: Arbitrary file read via ImageDocument.metadata["file_path"] in image_documents_to_base64
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 3 lines of code: ImageDocument(metadata={'file_path': '/etc/passwd'}) then image_documents_to_base64([doc]). Affects any RAG or multimodal-agent application that ingests user-influenced input into ImageDocument. Sensitive files readable include AWS credentials, K8s tokens, .env files. 15 comments from community confirming impact.

signals.topic: Missing `AgentStream.thinking_delta` when using Anthropic LLM with FunctionAgent streaming
signals.summary: FunctionAgent/AgentWorkflow streaming only reads thinking content from ChatResponse.additional_kwargs['thinking_delta']. When Anthropic streaming emits thinking deltas in provider-native fields but does not normalize them into additional_kwargs, thinking_delta is missing from the agent output stream. Users see empty thinking content.
aliases: Anthropic thinking blocks not forwarded to AgentStream
Thinking content dropped from workflow event stream
signals.review_reason: Clear UX degradation: users who pay for Anthropic's extended thinking capability see no thinking content in the streaming output. This undermines the value proposition of paying for thinking-enabled models. Not P0 because count=1 and the thinking content is still visible in the final response, just not streamed in real-time.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Missing AgentStream.thinking_delta when using Anthropic LLM with FunctionAgent
source_issues.evidence: With Anthropic streaming (thinking blocks/deltas), AgentStream.thinking_delta remains empty/missing in FunctionAgent output. The workflow code assumes thinking is in additional_kwargs['thinking_delta'] but Anthropic integration does not mirror it there.

signals.topic: LlamaParse v2 ignores `output_tables_as_markdown=true` and returns HTML tables instead of markdown

aliases: LlamaParse table output format not respected
HTML tables returned despite markdown table option
LlamaParse v2 output_options table setting broken

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LlamaParse v2 outputs HTML tables even with output_tables_as_markdown=true
source_issues.evidence: When output_tables_as_markdown=true is set in parsing options, HTML tables are still returned instead of markdown. Documented behavior not met. Breaks downstream markdown processing pipelines that expect proper markdown table formatting.

signals.topic: npm install fails silently — tool is completely uninstallable on Node 22, 25, and macOS 26
signals.summary: 用户在新版 Node.js (v22/v25) 和 macOS 26 上执行 `npm install -g ruflo` 或 `npx ruflo init` 时，npm 进程在依赖解析阶段静默崩溃（exit code 1），只输出通用错误信息，无任何可操作的诊断。根因是发布包中两个依赖（@claude-flow/mcp 和 agentic-flow）的 packument 返回 size:undefined 导致 npm resolver 崩溃。这完全阻断了新用户安装和主流程。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户完全无法安装工具，2 个独立 issue 均证明在 Node 22/25 和 macOS 26 上可稳定重现。npm 报错无任何可操作的诊断信息，是典型的静默失败导致主安装路径不可用。

source_issues.title: npm install -g ruflo@latest fails silently during dependency resolution — uninstallable on Node 22 & 25
source_issues.evidence: npm 进程在 idealTree buildDeps 阶段静默崩溃，exit code 1，无具体错误信息。@claude-flow/mcp 和 agentic-flow 返回 size:undefined 导致 resolver 崩溃。在 Node 22.22.2 和 v25.9.0 上均可重现，npx/npm/global 均失败。

source_issues.title: macbook instaltion
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告在 macOS 26 上无法安装，与 #1825 相同根因（npm install 失败）。

signals.topic: claude-flow 顶层包缺失运行时依赖 @claude-flow/cli-core，导致 npx claude-flow 启动即崩溃
signals.summary: 发布的 claude-flow 顶层包仅声明了 semver 和 zod 两个依赖，但打包了 CLI 的 dist 文件，该 dist 静态导入 @claude-flow/cli-core 等多个运行时包。npm 只安装 semver+zod，导致 Node.js 模块解析失败（ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND），所有 claude-flow 命令在执行任何用户逻辑前即崩溃。ruflo 依赖 @claude-flow/cli，后者本身有完整依赖所以不受影响，但直接使用 claude-flow 的用户路径完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: P0 判定：2 个独立 issue 均证明 claude-flow 主命令路径完全阻断，用户执行任何 CLI 子命令前即崩溃。虽然 ruflo 别名可用，但 claude-flow 是官方主包，依赖它的所有用户均受影响，是高优先级的包发布流程缺陷。

source_issues.title: claude-flow umbrella package missing required CLI runtime dependencies (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for @claude-flow/cli-core)
source_issues.evidence: claude-flow@3.7.0-alpha.8 顶层包仅声明 semver+zod，但 CLI dist 静态导入 @claude-flow/cli-core。Windows 新机器上 npx claude-flow 启动即崩溃，ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND。根因：顶层包打包了 @claude-flow/cli 的 dist 但未继承其 dependencies。作者已验证 3.7.0-alpha.9 修复。

source_issues.title: npx claude-flow fails with missing @claude-flow/cli-core
source_issues.evidence: Windows Node v22.16.0 上 npx claude-flow memory search 触发 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND @claude-flow/cli-core。与 #1795 同一根因（顶层包依赖缺失）。

signals.topic: Windows 后台 daemon 进程启动后立即退出 — 之前修复未完全解决 IPC channel 问题
signals.summary: v3.6.13 的 PR #1719 将 spawn 替换为 fork，但 Windows 上 daemon child 进程仍在父进程退出后立即死亡。根因：detached:false + IPC channel 组合下，child.unref() 无法关闭 IPC pipe，当 npx wrapper 退出时 Windows 销毁 IPC pipe 导致子进程退出。问题在 v3.6.30 仍存在（Issue #1766）。相关地，orphan swarms 在 daemon 重启间积累（Issue #1799），且 swarm_status 错误地将其报告为 healthy，加剧误导。
signals.review_reason: Windows 后台运行是核心功能（daemon start --background），已有之前修复但未完全解决，v3.6.30 仍复现。orphan swarms 导致运维监控给出错误状态（ghost swarm 被报告为 healthy），2 个 issue 同根因（Windows IPC/background 问题），影响 Windows 用户的核心使用路径。

source_issues.title: daemon start (background) still dies on Windows + Node 25 in v3.6.30 — IPC channel keeps fork tied to parent
source_issues.evidence: Windows 10 + Node v25.8.0，ruflo 3.6.30。daemon start 后 5 秒内子进程 PID 即消失。根因：fork + detached:false + stdio ipc + unref() 无法在 Windows 上让进程脱离父进程。已验证本地 patch（detached:true + disconnect()）有效。

source_issues.title: Orphan swarms accumulate in .claude-flow/swarm/swarm-state.json across daemon restarts
source_issues.evidence: Windows v3.7.0-alpha.8 上半天内积累 3 个 orphan swarms（status:running 但 agents:[], tasks:[]），由 daemon start 的 background 进程崩溃产生。swarm_status 继续将其列为 live，swarm_health 报告 healthy，严重误导运维判断。

signals.topic: Headless AI workers 运行成功但结果不持久化 — self-learning 功能形同虚设且浪费 Claude Code 费用
signals.summary: 当 Claude Code 可用时，daemon 选择 AI headless 模式运行 audit/optimize/testgaps 等 workers，输出结构化的 JSON 分析结果（12-44KB/次），但这些结果从未写入 .claude-flow/metrics/ 目录，memory store 也始终为空。hooks_intelligence_stats 显示 mode:local 而非 headless，导致 self-learning memory 和平台的自进化特性完全失效。用户支付了 Claude Code 费用但产出被丢弃。
aliases: metrics not written by headless mode
signals.review_reason: 功能核心承诺失效：self-learning memory 和 AI workers 自我进化是该产品的核心卖点，但 headless 结果完全不持久化。memory stats 始终为 0，用户支付 Claude Code tokens 但产出被丢弃在日志文件中。issue 提供了精确的根因代码位置（worker-daemon.ts runWorkerLogic headless 分支）和验证方法，有完整技术证据。count=1 但影响严重，标记 P1。

source_issues.title: Headless workers don't persist results — only raw logs/headless/ files; metrics/memory unchanged
source_issues.evidence: headlessExecutor.execute() 返回结果后直接返回，未调用 writeFileSync 写入 metrics/ 目录。local workers 路径则正确调用了 writeFileSync。hooks_intelligence_stats 显示 mode:local（与实际 headless 运行不符）。memory stats 报告 Total Entries: 0。用户支付 Claude Code 费用但结构化产出被丢弃在 logs/headless/。

signals.topic: Silent regressions: flashAttention 被硬编码为 false + ruvllm coordinator 使用错误包名导致性能特性静默失效
signals.summary: audit 发现了两个静默回归：(1) neural_status.features.flashAttention 返回硬编码 false，而 hooks_intelligence_stats 同时报告 implementation: real-flash-attention，两个数据源互相矛盾，用户无法察觉 Flash Attention 实际未启用；(2) 代码 require('@ruvector/ruvllm') 但 package.json 仅声明 @ruvector/ruvllm-wasm（无 @ruvector/ruvllm），require 静默失败并 fallback 到 JS-only 路径，性能特性丢失。系统不报任何错误，只在 dashboard 显示 unavailable。
signals.review_reason: 可信度/体验降级问题：文档声称的性能优化特性（Flash Attention 2.49-7.47× speedup、ruvllm Rust/Wasm 加速）实际上因代码问题完全未启用，且因为 try/catch 吞掉错误，没有任何告警。silent regression 性质恶劣——用户以为系统在工作，实际在回退路径上运行。count=1 但影响产品质量信誉，标记 P1。

source_issues.title: intelligence: two silent regressions — flashAttention hardcoded false + ruvllm coordinator package-name mismatch
source_issues.evidence: neural-tools.ts:699 硬编码 flashAttention: false 而非调用实际 loader。3 个文件 require('@ruvector/ruvllm') 但 npm 仅声明 '@ruvector/ruvllm-wasm'，require 静默失败走 JS fallback。hooks_intelligence_stats 和 neural_status 数据不一致。用户无法察觉性能降级。

signals.topic: agent-browser install command fails on Windows, blocking initial setup
signals.summary: Users on Windows cannot run `agent-browser install` — the command fails, leaving the browser binary uninstalled and the tool unusable. Screenshot evidence shows clear failure output.
signals.review_reason: Installation failure on a major platform blocks 100% of the user journey. The tool is completely unusable after install without the browser binary. Direct user evidence with screenshot confirms failure.

source_issues.title: The execution of the 'agent-browser install' command failed
source_issues.evidence: Screenshot shows install command failure on Windows. User explicitly states command does not execute successfully. No workaround provided.

signals.topic: Homebrew installation fails with 'playwright: command not found', preventing browser install
signals.summary: Users installing via Homebrew encounter a shell error when `agent-browser install` tries to call `playwright` — the playwright binary is not in PATH, causing install to abort and leaving the tool non-functional.
signals.review_reason: Homebrew is a primary distribution channel for macOS. Install failure leaves the tool completely unusable. The shell dependency on playwright not being in PATH is a clear packaging bug with confirmed user impact across multiple users (8 comments).

source_issues.title: bug: attempt to install the browser fails
source_issues.evidence: Shell error 'sh: playwright: command not found' produced during install. User installed via Homebrew and the install step failed. 8 comments indicate active community discussion and confirmed reproduction.

signals.topic: Windows Defender falsely flags agent-browser browser binary as Trojan and quarantines it, blocking install and runtime
signals.summary: During installation, Windows Defender detects the Chrome browser binary shipped by agent-browser as Trojan:Win32/Posilod.EB and quarantines it, making the tool completely unusable post-install. No way for users to distinguish false positive from real threat.
aliases: Windows Defender trojan detection quarantines browser binary
signals.review_reason: AV quarantine directly prevents the tool from functioning after installation — the browser binary is deleted by the OS. Users have no clear path to recovery (whitelisting a quarantined file is non-obvious). This blocks the entire user journey on Windows.

source_issues.title: Detected: Trojan:Win32/Posilod.EB!cl
source_issues.evidence: Windows Defender explicitly quarantined libGLESv2.dll inside the bundled Chrome binary. User cannot run agent-browser after install because the browser binary has been removed by the OS. Confirmed by user on Windows 11 Pro.

signals.topic: Regression: find role link --name silently fails after PR #1153 reverted the #1145 fix, breaking a core accessibility-tree command
signals.summary: The `find role link --name` command was fixed in PR #1145 using CDP accessibility tree but silently reverted by PR #1153, restoring a buggy JS selector that fails to match link elements. Users relying on this command for web scraping automation see silent failures with 'Element not found' errors.
aliases: role link selector broken after revert
signals.review_reason: Regression in a core command that previously worked correctly. The failure is silent (no error thrown, just 'Element not found'), making it especially disruptive for automation pipelines. A previous fix exists and was confirmed working, proving the regression is real and introduced by a specific commit.

source_issues.title: Regression: find role link --name fails again — PR #1145 fix reverted by PR #1153
source_issues.evidence: Bisect confirms the fix was reverted 5 hours after landing. Silent failure with 'Element not found' on a command that previously worked. Workarounds (find text, click @ref) exist but change the user workflow significantly.

signals.topic: session-setup does not pre-grant geolocation permissions in headless mode; prompts are silently skipped, breaking location-dependent automation
signals.summary: After session-setup, pages calling navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition() either silently skip the prompt or never fire the callback. Headless Chrome suppresses permission UI and without CDP pre-granting, geolocation is completely blocked. No error is shown to the user.
signals.review_reason: Geolocation is a commonly-used browser API for automation (testing location-based apps, ad verification, etc.). The failure is silent — no error thrown, just permission denied silently — making it very hard to diagnose. The workaround requires foreknowledge that users are unlikely to have, making this effectively a blocking issue for location-dependent automation.

source_issues.title: session-setup doesn't pre-grant geolocation; permission prompts skipped or silently fail
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed silent failure using browserleaks.com/geo as verification target. The only workaround requires users to proactively set geo override before opening the URL, which requires foreknowledge of the limitation. Location-dependent web automation is completely broken.

signals.topic: Zod 4.4.x breaking Bedrock and MCP tool calls — schema validation rejects missing `input` field and `resource_link` content type
signals.summary: Two distinct schemas in `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` and `@ai-sdk/mcp` broke with Zod 4.4.x because they declared fields as `z.unknown()` without `.optional()`, causing tool calls to fail silently at runtime validation.
signals.review_reason: count=2, 主流程阻断：Zod 4.4.x升级后两个包的工具调用流全部静默失败，错误在SDK内部触发而非用户代码，排查困难，影响所有使用Zod 4.4.x的Bedrock和MCP工具调用用户。

source_issues.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): BedrockToolUseSchema input field breaks with zod@4.4.x
source_issues.evidence: Type validation error: 'Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined' for contentBlockStart events where toolUse has no input field. Tool calls silently fail at streaming deserialization.

source_issues.title: BedrockToolUseSchema rejects valid contentBlockStart events under Zod >= 4.4.0
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause as #14930: Zod 4.4.x changed z.unknown() to reject missing keys. Tool calls broken for any consumer on Zod >= 4.4.1.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/anthropic: obsolete effort-2025-11-24 beta header rejected by Vertex AI, blocking effort feature on Vertex
signals.summary: @ai-sdk/anthropic auto-injects the stale beta header 'anthropic-beta: effort-2025-11-24' whenever the effort option is set. Since effort went GA on 2025-11-24, Vertex's strict validator now rejects this header with HTTP 400, completely blocking the effort feature for all Vertex users.
signals.review_reason: count=2, 主流程阻断：effort功能对Vertex用户完全不可用（HTTP 400），而出同样请求体直连Anthropic正常。两个相关issue（14766为fix PR，14833为support报告）均指向同一根因。

source_issues.title: fix(provider/anthropic): stop sending obsolete effort-2025-11-24 beta header (rejected by Vertex)
source_issues.evidence: Vertex returns HTTP 400: 'Unexpected value(s) effort-2025-11-24 for the anthropic-beta header'. Effort feature completely broken on Vertex. Issue filed as fix PR, confirmed with credential-free reproduction showing header injection.

source_issues.title: Vertex priority service tier + labels not propagated (direct provider rejects 'priority', Gateway BYOK drops both)
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly mentions the effort beta header rejection as part of the Vertex breakage; body confirms this is the same root cause.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google streaming parser drops no-args function calls, causing multi-turn agent conversations to 400 on Vertex
signals.summary: When Vertex sends a streaming function call with `name` but no `args`/`willContinue`/`partialArgs`, the streaming parser has no matching classifier branch and silently drops the entire call, losing the `thoughtSignature` that Vertex requires for multi-turn conversations.
signals.review_reason: 高频 + 主流程阻断：用户报告约50%的多轮对话会触发此bug，导致Agent下一步直接400失败，完全阻断多步Agent流程。AI Gateway路径同样受影响。根因清晰（parser无匹配分支），证据充分（wire-level抓包）。

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing thoughtSignature
source_issues.evidence: Vertex enforces rule: assistant turn with function calls must include thoughtSignature; parser drops first call when it has no args; response ends up with zero signatures; next agent step 400s with 'missing thought_signature'. Affects ~half of all multi-turn continuations. Both direct @ai-sdk/google and AI Gateway paths are broken.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/xai: Responses stream error events surface as TypeValidationError instead of provider error
signals.summary: xAI Responses API streams `type: 'error'` events on API failures, but @ai-sdk/xai validates them against the normal Responses event union, surfacing a massive Zod union error instead of the actual xAI error message, making debugging impossible.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：用户完全无法看到实际错误原因，只看到无意义的Zod验证错误栈，多步排查后仍未找到根因。虽非主流程阻断，但严重妨碍调试，影响xAI provider的可用性。

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/xai: Responses stream error events surface as TypeValidationError
source_issues.evidence: SDK throws AI_TypeValidationError with long Zod union error, completely obscuring xAI's actual error message ('Invalid arguments passed to the model.'). No workaround. Users cannot debug why tool schemas are rejected.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/togetherai: generateImage sends unsupported diffusion parameters to non-diffusion models, breaking image generation
signals.summary: TogetherAI image model always includes `seed` and optionally `steps`/`negative_prompt` in the request body, even when undefined. The Together AI API rejects these parameters for non-diffusion models like google/gemini-3-pro-image with 'Unsupported use of seed/steps parameter'.
signals.review_reason: 主流程失败：用户调用generateImage()即报错，指定的gemini-3-pro-image模型完全无法通过SDK使用。根因明确（seed/steps无条件包含在body中），有完整复现代码。

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/togetherai image model sends unsupported parameters to non-diffusion models (e.g. google/gemini-3-pro-image)
source_issues.evidence: generateImage() with google/gemini-3-pro-image throws AI_APICallError: 'Unsupported use of seed parameter' or 'Unsupported use of steps parameter'. Non-diffusion multimodal models cannot be used via the SDK. Full reproduction code provided.

signals.topic: Security: NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_HEADERS disables internal header filtering allowing header forgery attacks
signals.summary: The NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_HEADERS environment variable disables all internal header filtering in middleware. Attackers can forge internal headers (x-middleware-rewrite, x-middleware-redirect, x-middleware-cookie) to bypass middleware logic, trigger arbitrary redirects, and set arbitrary cookies.
signals.review_reason: P0 — Critical security vulnerability allowing authentication bypass, arbitrary redirects, and cookie injection via forged internal headers. Three duplicate reports confirm widespread real-world impact on production deployments.

source_issues.title: NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_HEADERS env var disables all internal header filtering
source_issues.evidence: Security: attackers can forge internal headers (x-middleware-rewrite, x-middleware-redirect, x-middleware-cookie) to bypass middleware logic, trigger arbitrary redirects, set arbitrary cookies.

source_issues.title: [Bug] NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_HEADERS env var disables all internal header filtering
