source_issues.title: [Bug] NEXT_PRIVATE_TEST_HEADERS env var disables all internal header filtering
source_issues.evidence: Same security issue as #93440 (duplicate report).

signals.topic: Browser back navigation after notFound()/404 leaves previous page detached and non-interactive
signals.summary: In App Router dev mode, after navigating to a notFound() or 404 page and pressing browser Back, the previous page's React tree becomes detached. All buttons are non-interactive, event handlers do not fire. The page is effectively broken until a full page reload.
aliases: navigating back from 404 leaves page broken
browser back breaks previous page dev
signals.review_reason: Broken user experience in navigation — back button leaves pages completely non-functional with no recovery except manual reload. Affects a core browser navigation flow used frequently by end users.

source_issues.title: App Router dev mode: browser Back after notFound() leaves previous page detached
source_issues.evidence: After notFound() and browser Back, previous page React tree becomes detached. Buttons non-interactive, no event handlers fire. Canary: 'Connection closed' x2 then auto-reload.

source_issues.evidence: After navigating to 404 and pressing Back, previous page loses all interactivity. Counter doesn't work, buttons don't respond, React state broken. F5 refresh restores. Dev-only; production works correctly.

signals.topic: Turbopack build crash in monorepo with Pages Router and externalDir
signals.summary: In Turbopack dev mode with monorepo setups using externalDir, the Pages Router _document page is omitted from build paths, causing PageNotFoundError during page data collection despite successful compilation. Build fails completely.
signals.review_reason: Blocking build failure in monorepo setups — page not found error prevents successful builds, clear user impact in selective Pages Router builds with Turbopack.

source_issues.title: Turbopack debug-build-paths omits Pages Router _document in monorepo externalDir app

signals.topic: Turbopack CPU spin and 4.9GB trace file crashes development server
signals.summary: Running next dev with Turbopack on App Router client pages causes CPU to spin, writes a 4.9GB trace-turbopack file, then HMR and route requests fail. Development is completely broken.
signals.review_reason: P0 — Complete development workflow breakage with massive resource consumption (4.9GB disk fill). Dev server becomes completely unresponsive, blocking all development activity on the affected project.

source_issues.title: next dev with Turbopack on App Router client page spins CPU, writes 4.9GB trace-turbopack, then HMR and route requests fail
source_issues.evidence: Dev server CPU spin, 4.9GB trace file written, HMR and route requests fail. Development completely broken.

signals.topic: Turbopack dynamic import() failures have no recovery path after transient errors
signals.summary: After a transient network failure, dynamic import() calls in Turbopack keep failing for seconds even after connectivity is restored. No retry mechanism exists. Only a full page reload restores functionality, destroying all in-memory state including React state and form data.
aliases: import() no retry after network failure
signals.review_reason: User impact: transient failures cause permanent state loss. Users must manually reload and lose all in-memory React state, form data, and navigation context. Common on flaky networks.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: dynamic import() failures stay failed - no recovery path without a full page reload
source_issues.evidence: After transient network failure, dynamic import() keeps failing for seconds even after connectivity restored. No retry mechanism. Only full page reload restores functionality, destroying in-memory state.

signals.topic: Command execution becomes extremely slow with high CPU usage in turbo 2.9.x
signals.summary: Multiple users report turbo 2.9.x causing extreme slowness with tokio-rt-worker processes consuming full CPU cores, blocking the build workflow. Regression from 2.9.3 to 2.9.8 confirmed.
signals.review_reason: Three confirmed bug reports with reproduction steps all pointing to the same root cause: turbo 2.9.x consuming 100% CPU during or after builds, blocking the primary build workflow. The 2.9.8 regression (issue #12703) is explicitly a main-flow slowdown with tokio-rt-worker CPU spike. Issue #8801 and #8122 are longer-standing daemon/CPU issues. All three have high comment counts indicating broad user impact.

source_issues.title: Command execution through turbo has become really slow
source_issues.evidence: tokio-rt-worker processes consume full CPU cores; reproduction repo provided; regression from 2.9.3 to 2.9.8; build that should take seconds takes minutes

source_issues.title: Extremely slow with 100% CPU usage

source_issues.title: Turbo daemon uses 100% CPU even when no tasks are running

signals.topic: Turbo daemon 100% CPU leak after task completion

signals.topic: turbo `affected` command fails to resolve base branch in GitHub Actions CI

aliases: affected command GitHub Actions base branch failure

source_issues.title: `affected` failing to resolve main branch in GitHub action

signals.topic: Turbo silently scans entire home directory and hangs when project has no .git folder
signals.summary: When turbo.json is in a directory without a .git folder but a parent directory has one (e.g. home dir), turbo recursively scans all files in the home directory causing indefinite hang with zero output.
aliases: silent hang no .git home directory scan
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow blocker: turbo hangs silently with no error/warning, consuming all system resources scanning the home directory. Users downloading repos as ZIPs (very common workflow) hit this consistently. The failure mode is extremely confusing with no diagnostic output. Clearly meets the '主流程失败/阻断' and '反复失败' criteria.

source_issues.title: Turbo silently scans entire home directory and hangs when project has no .git (ZIP download)

signals.topic: CLI env add --value silently stores empty string — production secrets/keys missing at runtime
signals.summary: The `vercel env add` command with `--value` flag silently stores an empty string instead of the provided value, reporting success while the variable is actually empty. Affects both plain `--value` (CLI 53.x) and `--value --sensitive` (since 50.5.0). This causes production deployments to run with missing API keys, HMAC failures, and broken auth with no CLI error.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：env var 是 CI/CD 自动化的核心操作，两条 issue 均描述同一命令路径（vercel env add --value）静默失败并返回误导性成功信息。用户只有在生产环境读不到 key 时才被动发现，此时已造成实际业务损失（HMAC 校验失败、API key 缺失）。两条 issue 来自不同用户、相同根因、去重后 count=2，满足 P0 高频+主流程阻断+有样例链接的条件。

source_issues.title: vercel env add: --value silently stored as empty string (CLI 53.x), and --sensitive empty since 50.5.0

Both produce misleading 'Added Environment Variable' success output while the actual value is empty. Pulls from env pull show NAME="". Causing broken HMAC verification, missing API keys in production.

signals.topic: @vercel/node TypeScript types claim Express-style helpers (res.status/json/send) that are absent in Rust Node runtime — causes TypeError in production after clean compile
signals.summary: The @vercel/node TypeScript types declare Express-style response helpers (res.status(), res.json(), res.send()) that do not exist at runtime in Vercel's Rust-based Node runtime. Code passes tsc --noEmit but throws 'TypeError: res.status is not a function' in production (HTTP 500).
aliases: VercelResponse Express helpers missing Rust runtime
signals.review_reason: 类型与运行时行为严重不一致：用户在本地通过 TypeScript 编译检查（tsc --noEmit），CI/CD 流程也显示构建成功，但生产环境在函数首次执行时崩溃返回 HTTP 500。Vercel Rust runtime 是当前的默认 runtime，res.status/res.json 是 Vercel 官方文档中的标准写法，用户覆盖面广。虽为单条 issue 但用户影响极其明确（生产阻断 + 500 错误），P1 合理。

source_issues.title: @vercel/node TypeScript types declare Express-style helpers (res.status, res.json) that are absent in the Rust Node runtime
source_issues.evidence: Code compiles cleanly with tsc --noEmit but throws TypeError: res.status is not a function in production on the Rust-based Node runtime (/opt/rust/nodejs.js in stack trace). signals.topic: macOS: Zed accumulates 100+ zombie child processes due to missing waitpid after SIGKILL in Drop handler
signals.summary: On macOS, Zed accumulates zombie child processes under the main Zed process (observed 100+ `<defunct>` children after a long-running session). The macOS `Drop` implementation for `Child` sends `SIGKILL` when `kill_on_drop` is set but never calls `waitpid` to reap the child. Language servers (LSP) are spawned with `kill_on_drop(true)`, so repeated LSP starts/stops accumulate unreaped zombies. Process table entries leak until Zed exits.
signals.review_reason: Critical system resource leak on macOS. Process table entries (a finite OS resource) accumulate indefinitely during normal Zed use. With repeated LSP restarts, the Zed process accumulates zombies that only clear on exit. This can eventually cause process table exhaustion, preventing Zed from spawning new processes. The author provided a precise root cause analysis with working test patch, making this a high-confidence, high-impact issue.

source_issues.title: macOS: killed child processes can remain as zombies because custom Command wrapper does not reap after SIGKILL
source_issues.evidence: macOS: '116 zombie children + 1 live crash-handler child' observed via ps after a long-running session. Root cause identified in crates/util/src/command/darwin.rs: Drop sends SIGKILL without waitpid. Reproduced with local patch and cargo tests. Affects LSP processes which use kill_on_drop(true).

signals.topic: Linux/Wayland: 'Awaiting Confirmation' spinner causes 47–50% iGPU render utilization and ~2W additional power draw
signals.summary: On Linux/Wayland with an integrated GPU only, Zed's 'Awaiting Confirmation' spinner (shown during AI agent tool call approval) causes the iGPU to render at 47–50% busy and draw an additional ~2W of power. Compared to idle state, the spinner triples GPU utilization and adds ~1.3W sustained draw. On laptops with only iGPU, this keeps the fan running and package temps elevated indefinitely while the user reads the screen.
signals.review_reason: Direct user cost: measurable battery drain (~2W additional) on laptops with iGPU-only systems during a very common interaction (AI agent confirmation spinner). This is a sustained power regression while users are reading the screen. The issue includes precise quantitative measurements (intel_gpu_top data) confirming the cause is Zed's own rendering, not the compositor. Significant UX degradation for laptop users on Linux.

source_issues.title: GPUI runs the iGPU at 47–50% Render busy to animate the agent 'Awaiting Confirmation' spinner
source_issues.evidence: Linux Wayland Ubuntu 26.04, Intel Iris Xe iGPU (only GPU). Detailed metrics: idle=16% render busy/0.69W, spinner=47-50%/~2.0W. dGPU confirmed uninvolved. kwin compositor contribution drops behind Zed during spinner frames. Spinner shown during agent tool call confirmation — a common interaction.
